main.Subject: AI Search: Indexed tags displayed in Facets
main.Description:
Hi Team,
Could you please explain what is the configuration/rule behind the tags displayed in the Filter Facets for AI Search in the ESC front-end portal?

We have AI Search enabled and indexed tags for the knowledge table - we actively use tags for our articles to allow users narrowing down content. 

I've noticed there are 10 tags shown in the facet - what is the rule for their selection? 

Thank you,
Karolina
main.Resolution notes:
[code]

Hello Karolina,

My name is Kavita, and I will assist you with your Case.

ISSUE: AI Search: Indexed tags displayed in Facets.

SOLUTION PROPOSED:
Q1: Could you please explain what is the configuration/rule behind the tags displayed in the Filter Facets for AI Search in the ESC front-end portal?

  • Tags from source records can be indexed based on their visibility, with options for indexing shared and globally visible tags.

  • As referenced in the documentation below, AI Search can index tags directly from source table records. Additionally, search results display these indexed tags based on the visibility of the result record itself, rather than the visibility of the individual tag.

  • This means that if a user has access to the record, the associated tags may also appear in search results, even if the tag's visibility is restricted.

    Key References:

    Field settings for AI Search: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/bundle/zurich-platform-administration/page/administer/ai-search/concept/field-settings-ais.html

    Indexed source attributes: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/bundle/yokohama-platform-administration/page/administer/ai-search/concept/indexed-source-attributes-ais.html

    Managing access to knowledge bases: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/bundle/zurich-servicenow-platform/page/product/knowledge-management/concept/user-access-knowledge-bases.html

    Indexing content from AI Search indexed sources:
    https://www.servicenow.com/docs/bundle/yokohama-platform-administration/page/administer/ai-search/concept/indexing-content-ais.html

    Indexed source attributes for AI Search: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/ai-search/indexed-source-attributes-ais.html?section=enable-tag-indexing-ais

Q2: I've noticed there are 10 tags shown in the facet - what is the rule for their selection?

  • The portal UI will typically display a limited number of facet values. So the 10 tags you see in the facet are not globally all tags, but the top 10 based on relevance/frequency for the current set of indexed articles and your search result context.

  • Please review this community Article on how to add facets for tags and emphasizes facets come from indexed fields and the search source configuration. This suggests the behavior is tied to how facets are defined, not how many values are shown.
    https://www.servicenow.com/community/intelligence-ml-forum/create-facets-for-tags/m-p/324431

NEXT STEPS: I will now place this case into a 'Solution Proposed' state. If you have any further questions, please let me know. Otherwise, please kindly archive this Case.

main.Subject: We are implementing AI search. Partial record searches return zero results
main.Description: Another AI search related case, CS8994036 was just resolved. Now that AI search is active, partial record searches return zero results.
main.Resolution notes:
Hello Mark,

I reviewed this issue further with my internal team.

We reviewed and unfortunately found that this is expected behavior.

AI Search is designed to return results based on relevance and intent, using keyword, semantic, or hybrid search models. Because of this design, AI Search does not support guaranteed partial matching for record identifiers such as Incident Numbers.

AI Search for incident numbers only work when users enter the full Incident Number (for example, INC0012345).
Searches using only a partial Incident Number (such as 12345 or INC001) may return results in some situations, but this behavior is not reliable or consistent.

Recommended approach

For best results in AI Search, users should search using the complete Incident Number.
If consistent partial‑number searching is required (for example, searching by the last few digits of an Incident Number), classic list views or filters should be used instead of AI Search.

Here is a link to some documentation that goes over fuzzy number AI search that also explains how AI search works.

Link: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/ai-search/fuzzy-numeric-search.html

With this I will now place this case in Solution Proposed state.

Please click the "Accept Solution" button to close out this case if you have no further questions.

ご報告いただいた事象につきまして御社開発環境の devatcsupport にて確認した結果、
原因はご認識の通りに、sn_customerservice_case テーブルに対する AI Data Source（ais_datasource） の indexed source に設定された filter 条件により、index 対象レコードが制限されている点にあることを確認いたしました。

そのため、「この記事の下書きを作成するためのタスクを検索」の処理では、検索可能なレコード範囲が限定され、検索結果が取得できない状態となっていたと考えられます。

対応方針として indexed source を調整する方向性は適切ですが、ServiceNow platform には以下の制約がございます。

  • 1つのテーブルに対して作成できる indexed source は最大1件まで

https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/ai-search/create-indexed-source-ais.html

  • 既存の sn_customerservice_case の indexed source から filter 条件を削除し、case レコード全体を index 対象とする
  • その後 reindex を実行する

つまり、indexed source は「最大範囲の検索対象」を定義し、実際の検索条件は各 search source で絞り込む形となります。

main.Subject: Urgent: Performance Alert – Multiple Node Restarts Detected Due To Out-Of-Memory Errors
main.Description: Multiple Out Of Memory errors detected
main.Resolution notes:
[code]

Hi Nicholas Waterman,

We are placing this case in Solution Proposed.
Please note that moving the case to a Solution Proposed state does not close the case and you still have the ability to update the case with any comments or questions, which myself and my colleagues will see and can reply to you accordingly.

Reason:
We have found the main cause of the performance degradation along with some recommendations to prevent an reocurrance of this issue.

Issue Summary:
Our proactive monitoring detected that instance, libertymutual, alerted at 08:00 am PST due to Multiple node restarts caused by Out-Of-Memory errors.

Solution Proposed:

  1. ServiceNow engineers identified that the main cause of the node restarts was due to the AIS Index Event Processor job
  2. We worked with one of our internal teams to understand why the AIS Index Event Processor job caused the memory pressure across the nodes. We discover that the main cause was due to a high number of ais_index events generated from updates to fields on change_request & sn_hr_core_profile tables. The event count jumped at around 07:00 am PST and the queue size grew up to tens of thousands of events, reaching peaks of over 60 000 events, which is what we suspect led to the memory pressure on the nodes that processed AIS index events.
  3. We identified a set of columns where we need to enable the "no_text_index" attribute. Enabling this attribute will prevent the creation of these events and will avoid memory pressure on the nodes.
    1. fields from change_request table
      a. conflict_last_run
      b. conflict_status
      c. sys_mod_count
      d. sys_update_by
    2. fields from sn_hr_core_profile table
      a. national_tax_id_encrypted
      b. sys_mod_count
      c. sys_updated_by
      d. sys_update_by

Recommendations to prevent future impact:

  1. Navigate to: AI Search > AI Search Index > Indexed Sources
    or point your browser to: https://libertymutual.service-now.com/ais_datasource_list.do?sysparm_query=&sysparm_view=
  2. Open the record for Source=change_request
  3. On the form, click on the 'Field Settings & Mapping' tab
  4. Click the 'New' button
  5. On the new record form, set the following fields:
    Field: conflict_last_run
    Attribute: no_text_index
    Value: true
  6. Click 'Submit' button to add the record.
  7. Repeat steps 3-6 for the other remaining change_request fields: conflict_status, sys_mod_count, sys_update_by
  8. Open the Indexed Source [ais_datasource] record for sn_hr_core_profile table
  9. Repeat steps 3-6, but for the sn_hr_core_profile fields: national_tax_id_encrypted, sys_mod_count, sys_updated_by, sys_updated_on

These steps will help to prevent future occurrences of the memory pressure caused by frequent updates to both the change_request & sn_hr_core_profile and will no longer generate an excessive number of ais_index events


Next Steps:
Nicholas, it was a pleasure working with you. Please review the information provided and accept the solution to close this case or let me know if you have any other inquiry or concern, I will be happy to clarify any doubts or questions.

You may receive a survey for this case after closure. I would really appreciate your feedback by filling the survey. It is important for me and ServiceNow to provide excellent quality of service and your feedback will allow us to continually improve it.

Thank you,

Carlos Hernandez
Performance team

Can we directly index the content of the mykcbenefits.com site ? → No — AI Search cannot directly index from public website by URL. What is supported is ingesting external content via an integration. ServiceNow officially supports three ingestion models for external content: Search Connector applications (SharePoint, Confluence, etc.) Custom integrations using Flow Designer + AI Search Spoke External Content REST APIs (push model) In all cases: The external system must expose content in a consumable API format AI Search indexes what you send, not what exists on the site itself Here is some documentation for the AIS search external sources that you can review: Link: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/ai-search/external-content-ais.html 2. Where is indexed content stored in servicenow under which table → Please review this article as it goes over how external content works in AI search Link: https://www.servicenow.com/community/intelligence-ml-articles/how-to-bring-external-content-into-ai-search/ta-p/2497286 As mentioned in the above article: "The external content schema table does not store data in the database. Instead, its columns serve as a map of AI Search index fields to populate when you index content from external data sources. " 3. If there is a missing content , can we manaully add an entry in that ? → No — you cannot manually add or edit indexed external content inside ServiceNow. This is because as mentioned above there is no table record to insert or modify. The index is populated only through ingestion events. The only supported way to add missing content is to: Fix the upstream source (API response completeness) and than re‑index 4. Please share any architectural details around how AI search works behind the scenes. → Here is some documentation that goes over how AI search architecture works. PLease review Link: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/yokohama/platform-administration/ai-search/explore-ais-architecture.html With this, I will now place this case in Solution Proposed state. main.Resolution notes: sasaki 様 いつもお世話になっております。テクニカルサポートのHenryです。 お問合せに回答致します。 [code]お問合せ内容:[/code] （CS9021304から分割）AI Search関連する質問について [code]回答:[/code] > Q1： > 検索結果の表示順についてデフォルトだと「関連性」順とのことですが > 関連性はどのようにはかられたものでしょうか。 > 関連する製品ドキュメント： > https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/yokohama/platform-administration/ai-search/sort-options-srch-app-cfg-ais.html 回答： AI Searchは、機械学習ベースの関連性モデルを使用して検索結果のスコアを算出し、スコアの高い順に結果を表示します。 この関連性モデルは、ユーザーの検索操作やクリック履歴などのインタラクションを学習し、自動的に精度を改善します。 ただし、機械学習アルゴリズム自体は非公開であり、関連性モデルの精度を直接カスタマイズ（精度を弱める・強めるなど）することはできません。 <参考資料> - AI Search における機械学習の関連性 https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/ja-JP/platform-administration/ai-search/machine-learning-relevancy-ais.html 機械学習の関連性は自動的に有効になり、構成することはできません。("Machine learning relevancy is automatically enabled and isn't configurable.") - AI Search: Score Calculation https://support.servicenow.com/kb?id=kb_article_view&sysparm_article=KB1517598 > Q2： > また、検索にはAI Searchが使われているかと思うのですが > AI Searchを用いて検索が行われた場合は、 > KB検索する際に、検索ワードが、メタ・タイトル・本文に入っていると検索結果として表示される認識で合っていますでしょうか。 回答： ご認識のとおり、特に OOB の設定変更が行われていない場合、 kb_knowledge の上記情報は既に AI Search のインデックス処理に含まれています。 <参考資料> https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/ja-JP/platform-administration/ai-search/indexed-sources-ais.html https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/ja-JP/platform-administration/ai-search/field-settings-ais.html 上記回答を持ちまして、本件のステータスをSolution Proposedとさせていただきます。 本件について、ご不明な点等ございましたらお気軽にお問合せください。 問題ないようでしたら、Accept Solutionを押下し本件をクローズして頂けますと幸いです。 以上、よろしくお願いいたします。 Henry Lee | Technical Support, APJ Delivery Services

SOLUTION PROPOSED: 
Lucia's March 30th email contains all the details as customer  requested.

The call focused on how to reduce the number of search results returned by the ESC search profile (from the default value of 12 to a lower, desired number) and whether this can be done without cloning the existing search profile/widget, which is currently in use.

Key discussion points
1. Cloning the search profile (best practice)
Cloning the search application / search profile is the recommended best practice when customising the search experience, as this prevents unintended impact on other portals (e.g. ESC, EIC) that may rely on the same profile.
While a direct modification could technically be tested, this approach is not recommended when the search profile is actively used by a portal.
Since the search profile is currently in use by FiberCop, modifying it directly is not advised, as it could affect search behaviour in other contexts.

2. FiberCop concern about cloning
FiberCop explained that cloning the profile would impact existing KPIs and filters already configured on the current profile.
For a limited improvement (fewer search results), the effort and potential side effects of cloning were considered not worth the trade‑off.
FiberCop therefore asked whether any alternative approach could avoid cloning altogether. 

3. Testing without cloning
It was mentioned that to see whether the user experience remains acceptable.
However, the profile is used by a portal, cloning remains the safest and supported approach. 

4. Alternative workaround (manual, not upgrade‑safe)
An alternative option was mentioned: modifying the widget directly with help from the CSM/Dev team to control how many results are displayed.
This approach: 
Is manual
Must be re‑applied after every upgrade or widget update
Is not automatically preserved across releases
This makes it a viable but non‑standard solution, with higher operational overhead. 

5. Result Improvement Rules
FiberCop asked for clarification on "result improvement rules."
Shared the following for reference 
https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/ai-search/result-improvement-rules-ais.html
These rules: 
Allow boosting specific results based on keywords in the search query
Are configured manually, by identifying keywords and mapping them to preferred results/documents
Do not change the number of results, but improve relevance and ordering
Documentation on how to configure these rules was (or would be) shared. 

Conclusions
Best practice remains cloning the search profile if the goal is to safely customise search behaviour without impacting other portals.
Direct modification without cloning is discouraged when the profile is in active use.
Manual widget modification is possible but requires ongoing maintenance at every release.
Result improvement rules can help improve relevance via keywords but do not replace cloning for structural changes.

Best regards,
Abhishek Methi

ServiceNow: No. The kb_home page is a core Knowledge Management page, and ServiceNow does not provide an OOB method to disable it. However, the page can technically be restricted through customizations such as: -> Removing knowledge roles from users -> Creating UI Builder custom home pages -> Hiding navigation modules -> Redirecting users via UI Script / Client Script But these would be custom solutions, not supported OOB configurations. Customize the Home page in UI Builder: Create a custom homepage and remove the Knowledge component. 3. Navigation control: Hide or restrict Knowledge modules from the Application Navigator. Currently, ServiceNow does not provide an OOB configuration to disable the Knowledge Home (kb_home) page or remove the Knowledge card from the Next Experience Home page (/now/nav/ui/home). The Knowledge link appears automatically for users who have Knowledge roles, and the behavior is controlled by the Now Experience Home components. If required, this behavior can only be altered through customization such as creating a custom homepage in UI Builder or modifying role access. main.Subject: AI Search Genius result not working
main.Description: We have enabled AI Search on our service portal and we are unable to view Genius Results
main.Resolution notes:
[code]

Hello,

We are placing this into Solution Proposed as we believe the information provided below will resolve your issue. If you have any questions or need anything else related to this Case, kindly contact us or update the case and we will be happy to assist you further. If this resolves your issue, please consider closing the Case by clicking on "Accept Solution".


REASON FOR SOLUTION PROPOSED:
The root cause has been identified and the customer has confirmed that Genius Results are now appearing after implementing the resolution steps.

ISSUE:
AI Search was enabled on the service portal, but Genius Results were not being displayed when performing searches (e.g., "password reset"). The issue was reproducible both in the service portal and in Search Preview as the maintenance user, while searches in French (Canada) returned Genius Results without issue, isolating the problem to the English language configuration.

ROOT CAUSE:
Investigation revealed that the English locale was not supported by the embedding model in use. Specifically, the field E5FT_body_dpr was empty because all of its locales ([en]) were not supported by the model E5FT. This was traced back to a corrupted or customized sys_language record for English, which caused the BGE Reranker to fail during Synthesized Answer Generation, logged as:

  • SEVERE: Errors encountered during BGE Reranking for Synthesized Answer Generation
  • WARNING: BGE Reranker not invoked because there are no valid execution requests, this could be a retrieval issue!

SOLUTION:
The issue was resolved by repairing the Core i18n plugin and re-indexing the AI Search sources:

  1. Repair the Core i18n plugin (com.glide.i18n.core) via the Plugin Manager on the affected instance.
  2. Once the plugin repair completes, re-index all AI Search indexed sources associated with the relevant search profile (e.g., catalog and KB sources).
  3. Verify that Genius Results are now appearing in the service portal and Search Preview.

The customer confirmed that after completing the above steps, Genius Results are appearing and working correctly for the Now Assist Virtual Agent.

NEXT STEPS:

  1. Verify that Genius Results continue to appear consistently across searches in the service portal.
  2. If the issue recurs or Genius Results stop appearing again, please update this case and we will be happy to assist further.
  3. If any other instances (e.g., TEST, PROD) are affected, repeat the plugin repair and re-indexing steps on those instances as well.

Please let us know if there is anything else we can assist you with.

Kind regards,

Justin Berger
Technical Support Engineer
Working Hours: 11:00 AM – 8:00 PM EST

[/code]

main.Resolution notes:
Hello Akash,

We are placing this case in a Solution Proposed state and will include a summary of your case details for our records. 

ISSUE: 

When indexing in dhlsparkexpdev1, for the Case/Knowledge/Users table is taking more time to complete, whereas indexing in dhlsparkexpsbox is getting completed faster than dhlsparkexpdev1. 

SOLUTION PROPOSED: 

We reviewed the indexing for the mentioned tables and both instances and found the following: 

First checking the example provided there was a recent large index for the Case table on dhlsparkexpdev1. 

Compare this to other indexing events that were completed in the dhlsparkexpsbox instance there are long running indexing events that took place as well as you can see on Feb 18th. 

Another observation we made is that the indexed source for the Case table you shared in your example has no filter conditions in dhlsparkexpdev1 while there are filter conditions for State is not one of closed or cancelled which will significantly reduce the number of records indexed as it is such a large table. 

The knowledge table appears to have some longer indexing occur for the most recent ingestions for dhlsparkexpdev1 when you were also running other indexing events for the long running Case table which will effect the indexing duration when you try indexing multiple tables at the same time. 

For the recent User indexed source indexing in dhlsparkexpdev1 there is no comparable recent indexing for the latest indexing event. 

In dhlsparkexpsbox the most recent indexing was completed in August so this is not a viable comparison however we are historically seeing long running index events in dhlsparkexpsbox so this seems to be consistent with what we see on dhlsparkexpdev1. 

NEXT STEPS: 

From our analysis this doesn't appear to be a problem in dhlsparkexpdev1 and is working as expected. 

Please let us know if you need any further clarification and we will be happy to help. 

Otherwise feel free to accept the solution to close out the case if no further assistance is needed.  

Best regards,
Brendan

main.Subject: Ensure that when a user searches for a Service or Service Offering, the search returns only catalog items where that service is actually available to that user, respecting the same access logic used when populating the catalog item variables.
main.Description: Please see for detailed question and steps tried into the attached document.
main.Resolution notes:
Hello Dionysis Giannaropoulos,

Thank you for your patience while we investigated this. We are placing this case in a Solution Proposed state as we have provided guidance regarding the limitations of AI Search for your use case.

AFFECTED INSTANCES: SNC Instance - vionet, SNC Instance - vionetdev, SNC Instance - vionettest.

ISSUE: A request for a supported method in AI Search to dynamically filter search results for catalog items based on user-specific access to Services or Service Offerings contained within the item's variables. The current implementation using static keywords in the meta field returns items that the user cannot actually use, creating misleading results.

SOLUTION PROPOSED: Investigation confirmed that the desired functionality, which requires dynamic, user-specific filtering of search results at query time, is a platform-level limitation in AI Search. The platform does not currently support indexing or filtering based on dynamic script includes or complex user criteria logic applied to catalog item variables.

Specifically, it was determined that:
1.  The `cmdb_ci_service` and `service_offering` tables are excluded from AI Search indexing by default, which prevents dot-walking to these fields for search filtering. While a system property (`glide.ais.ingestion.should_index`) exists, its should be thoroughly tested.

2.  Indexing of catalog item variables is only supported for specific variable types, such as 'Multiple choice' and 'Select box'. The variables in use, which reference the CMDB tables, are not among the supported types for indexing.

3.  The Search Scripted Post-processor feature is designed for transforming or enriching result data (e.g., reformatting dates) and does not support the removal of individual results based on runtime logic.

This functionality is considered an enhancement request for the platform.

NEXT STEPS: Please review the provided documentation links regarding AI Search limitations. For the desired functionality, we recommend submitting an enhancement request via the Ideas Portal on the ServiceNow Community.

Please let me know if you have any questions by updating this case.

Best regards,
Galimbek Sagidenov

To enable users to search for knowledge articles in any language, you can define an encoded query as the value of the 'glide.ais.global_searchable_filter.kb_knowledge' system property. Records that match this query are globally searchable, meaning they bypass the normal language filters and can be matched regardless of the search's language. As an example, a user searching from a German user session can match English or Japanese knowledge articles as long as they match the encoded query.

You can read additional details in the below documentation:

[Solution Proposed]
以下に回答いたします。
事象 :
Search retrievalツールの設定において、「Document matching threshold」を「1」に設定しているにもかかわらず、実際のアクション実行時に、関連度スコアが閾値を下回る（例：0.8）ナレッジ記事が検索結果として取得されてしまいます。

Note: 
a) To access the portal, please impersonate as 09444715.
b) For production access, the user should be part of this group - https://pepsico.service-now.com/sys_user_group.do?sys_id=3f666b70971ebe54bec13ae8c253afa8&sysparm_record_target=sys_user_group&sysparm_record_row=5&sysparm_record_rows=5&sysparm_record_list=nameCONTAINSs%26t+km%5Esys_id%21%3D38ea8d9ec3013010fd385b12b940dda3%5EORDERBYDESCsys_updated_on
main.Resolution notes: Hello Ashutosh, We are placing this case in a Solution Proposed state . AFFECTED INSTANCES: pepsicopp. ISSUE: Improve the search experience when search term contains "+" symbol. SOLUTION PROPOSED: In AI Search, during the lemma normalization phase, special characters like "+" are stripped because the tokenizer treats them as non-word characters. This is why "pep+" and "pep" produce the same results — the "+" is removed before any matching occurs. You can refer to the below documentation for more clarification:- https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/washingtondc/platform-administration/ai-search/lemma-unicode-normalization-ais.html NEXT STEPS: Please let me know if you have any questions by updating this case. main.Subject: AI Search is returning slow results intermitently
main.Description: AI Search takes 30 to 45 seconds to return a result (intermittently)
main.Resolution notes:
Hi CCEP Team,

Thanks for the continued patience as I investigated on this case. I was able to reproduce this while impersonating user Paul Johnson (on my first search only, search was instantaneous after the first search, you can easily reproduce this while on incognito mode)

Based on our investigation the observed delay during the initial AI Search query in the Service Portal is most likely due to cache initialization, which explains why the slowness only occurs on the first attempt. 

By default, AI Search uses early binding, where access controls (ACLs) are evaluated as part of the query itself, which can add overhead during the initial execution.
As a potential optimization, our development has recommended in the past to enabling late binding. In this approach, the search query retrieves results first and then applies ACL filtering afterward. 

While this method is generally more computationally intensive, it has been shown to improve initial search performance. However, one trade-off is that users may see fewer results per page than expected, as inaccessible records are filtered out after the query is executed. 

For additional details, please refer to the product documentation: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/bundle/xanadu-platform-administration/page/administer/ai-search/concept/content-security-ais.html

main.Subject: AI search displays "no records found" despite relevant KB articles appearing in the search results
main.Description:
AI search displays "no records found" despite relevant KB articles appearing in the search results and when we click on Ask a follow up it throws the below error.

As per our observation these issues appear sometimes and mostly when the search article has acronyms in the search or symbols like "/" or "[" or "]" etc.

Please find the attached document for more details
main.Resolution notes:
[code]

Hello Chaitanya,

Thank you for your patience while I investigated this further. I am now moving your case to Solution Proposed, as I believe the following information explains the behavior and gives the supported out-of-box path forward.

Issue

AI Search in the portal intermittently shows a Now Assist / Q&A card saying "There are no records found" even though relevant Knowledge results are listed below, and Ask a follow-up throws an error. From your examples, this is most reproducible when the query contains acronyms and/or special characters such as /, [ , ], hyphens, etc.

Root Cause

This does not look like a Knowledge visibility issue. It is more consistent with portal AI Search / Now Assist query handling:

  • In portal AI Search, exact match is not supported, so punctuation-heavy or acronym-heavy strings are not handled as strict literal terms. That can cause the standard result list to still return broad matches while the Now Assist Q&A layer fails its relevancy check and responds with no records found. Service Portal AI Search UX Troubleshooting Guide, Now Assist in AI Search FAQ
  • ServiceNow guidance on AI Search also notes that special characters can be reduced during normalization/indexing, which matches what you demonstrated with acronym/symbol-based queries. AI Search Unable to search special characters in Global search in Portal
  • For Ask a follow-up, ServiceNow's portal troubleshooting guidance states that this feature is only supported when the portal is configured with Enhanced Chat and the correct assistant EVAM / payload is present. If that OOB wiring is missing or incomplete, the follow-up action can fail. Service Portal AI Search UX Troubleshooting Guide

Proposed OOB Solution

  1. Do not rely on special characters or punctuation as searchable terms in portal AI Search / Now Assist.

    For affected articles, use a plain-text searchable version of the phrase in the article title/body/metadata, and include the expanded form of acronyms directly in the content. Example: include both the acronym and the full business term in the article so the normalized query still has strong matching terms. This is the supported OOB way to improve retrieval when portal exact-match behavior is not available. Service Portal AI Search UX Troubleshooting Guide, AI Search Unable to search special characters in Global search in Portal

  2. Re-test with normalized queries (remove /, [, ], hyphens, and search using full words rather than acronym-only phrases).

    Your own screenshots already show that when the acronym/special-character portion is removed, the Q\&A result behaves normally, which strongly supports query normalization as the trigger. Now Assist in AI Search FAQ, Service Portal AI Search UX Troubleshooting Guide

  3. Validate the OOB Now Assist portal prerequisites for "Ask a follow-up":

    • The portal must be enabled with Enhanced Chat.
    • The Search Profile must include the correct Now Assist Genius Result configuration.
    • The portal EVAM must use the correct Multi Content Portal Response Bundle / assistant mapping.
    • In the request payload, confirm vaEVAMDefinitionId is present, and in the returned Genius Result payload confirm vaEVAMItem exists. ServiceNow explicitly lists these checks for follow-up failures.
    • Confirm these key properties remain in the supported state:
      • glide.search.evam.use_legacy_template_generation = false
      • glide.ais.query.disable_async_mode = false (if the property exists)
      • sn_ais_assist.dpr_ingestion_completed = true

Important Note

At this time, I do not see an out-of-box setting that forces portal Now Assist to treat punctuation-heavy strings as exact-match literal queries. Based on ServiceNow's documented behavior, the supported OOB approach is to normalize the searchable content and ensure the portal Now Assist configuration is complete. Service Portal AI Search UX Troubleshooting Guide, AI Search Unable to search special characters in Global search in Portal

Official Supporting Documentation

  • Service Portal AI Search UX Troubleshooting Guide (KB2671620)
  • Now Assist in AI Search FAQ
  • AI Search special-character normalization discussion referencing official docs
  • Set minimum search terms for Now Assist Q&A
  • AI Search typo handling documentation

I'm placing the ticket in Solution Proposed. Please review the notes and consider closing this case by clicking Accept Solution.

You may receive a survey once the case is closed. We would really appreciate your feedback—it helps us continue improving the quality of our service.

If you need anything else related to this case, feel free to reach out and we'll be happy to assist further.

Should you prefer to speak with someone directly, please refer to our support contact page:

Support Contact Page

[/code]

main.Subject: Styling Limitation in the Service Portal "Portal Banner" Widget
main.Description:
Short Description:

The Portal Banner widget in the ServiceNow Service Portal, which uses the Typeahead widget when AI Search is active, presents a styling limitation affecting the search combobox. When custom CSS variables are applied at the :root level, only the border‑radius values are reflected. Attempts to modify the input background color, input appearance (color and radius), button color, and hover color do not take effect. As a result, the component shows only partial customization, retaining its default out‑of‑box color styling.

 

Description

The Portal Banner widget in the ServiceNow Service Portal is exhibiting a styling limitation when the Typeahead widget is used as part of the search experience, which occurs when AI Search is active. The search combobox within this component does not fully respond to custom CSS variables that are applied at the :root level. Although the defined variables successfully update the border‑radius, the widget does not apply changes to several other intended styling attributes.

Specifically, attempts to modify the input background color, input appearance (color and radius), button color, and hover color have no visible effect. Despite defining multiple --now-button-* variables and other CSS customizations, the combobox UI continues to display its default out‑of‑box design. The search field, along with the embedded icon button, retains the standard ServiceNow styles without reflecting the color adjustments configured in the custom stylesheet.

Because of this behavior, the Portal Banner shows only partial customization, where adjustments to the button shape—such as rounded corners—are correctly applied, but all color‑based customizations remain unchanged. This creates an inconsistency in the visual design, especially in environments where AI Search is enabled and the Typeahead widget replaces the traditional search element. The inability to override these styles results in limited flexibility for brand alignment and UI consistency within the Service Portal.

Link: 

https://bakerdex.service-now.com/bh_cordant

 

This issue can be classified as a Medium priority.

Reasoning:

The Portal Banner widget is functioning as expected in terms of search capability, so there is no impact to core functionality.
However, the styling limitation affects UI consistency, branding, and user experience, especially when AI Search is active and the Typeahead widget is used.
The inability to apply color styling may impact the visual alignment with corporate standards, making it important but not service‑blocking.
main.Resolution notes:

main.Subject: Clarification on usefulness of Meta Keywords field with AI Search enabled for Knowledge Articles
main.Description:
Hi Team,

We would like to seek clarification regarding the relevance and effectiveness of maintaining a Meta Keywords field on the Knowledge Article form, especially in our current setup where AI Search and Now Assist capabilities are already enabled.

As per our understanding, AI Search primarily processes and indexes the article body content, along with other contextual signals, to deliver relevant search results. Given this, we would like to understand:

Does the Meta Keywords field still play a significant role in improving search relevance or ranking when AI Search is enabled?
Is the Meta field actively used in indexing or retrieval by AI Search, or is it mainly applicable for legacy search configurations?
Would maintaining Meta Keywords provide any measurable improvement in:
- Article discoverability
- Search ranking
- Result accuracy
Are there any best practices or recommendations from ServiceNow on whether to:
Continue using Meta Keywords
Deprecate it in favor of AI-driven content understanding
If retained, what is the recommended way to generate or maintain these keywords (manual vs automated via Now Assist or scripting)?

Additionally, we are exploring whether to automate metadata generation for articles and want to ensure alignment with platform best practices.

Looking forward to your guidance.
main.Resolution notes:
[code]

Hello Kamlesh,

I am now moving your case to Solution Proposed, as I believe the following information will help resolve the problem.

Issue
Clarification on the usefulness of the Meta Keywords field with AI Search enabled for Knowledge Articles

Root Cause
This is partially possible OOB, but not by assigning a direct manual weight specifically to the meta field. In AI Search, relevancy is calculated by the platform's built-in ranking model and ML behavior, and ServiceNow explicitly states that AI Search does not use a configurable "field weight" model like Zing. However, tags/meta are part of the relevancy signals ("keyword match" / "keyword popularity"), so meta values can influence ranking if the field is indexed and searchable. AI Search FAQ, Content Creation for Relevancy in AI Search

Proposed OOB Solution

  • Make sure the meta field on kb_knowledge is included as a searchable field in the knowledge indexed source.

In AI Search, field settings control whether a field is searchable or excluded from search. Navigate to AI Search > AI Search Index > Indexed Sources, open the Knowledge indexed source, and add/configure the meta field so it is not excluded from search. Field settings for AI Search, Set up a field configuration for an indexed source

  • Run a full reindex of the knowledge indexed source after the field change.

ServiceNow documents that changes to indexed source field settings require a full table reindex to take effect for existing records. Field settings for AI Search, Indexing content from AI Search indexed sources

  • Verify your Service Portal search experience is using the correct AI Search source/profile/application.

AI Search is supported in Service Portal, and the search experience is driven by Search Sources, Search Profiles, and Search Application Configurations. The search profile is also where you manage synonyms and result-improvement behavior. AI Search Quick Start Guide, Configure the Experiences in AI Search

  • If you need stronger/top placement for certain keyword scenarios, use a Result Improvement Rule.

Because AI Search does not provide a direct manual field-weight control for meta, the supported OOB way to push specific results higher is to use Result Improvement Rules in the Search Profile:

Boost = raise relevancy for matching results
Promote = force specific results to appear first
Block = exclude unwanted results

These rules override the default ranking/order when triggered. Result improvement rules, Create a result improvement rule

  • Optionally add Synonym Dictionary entries for user/business terminology.

Search profiles support synonym dictionaries, and ServiceNow recommends synonyms to improve recall for organization-specific terms, acronyms, or alternate wording that may not exist in the title/description. Configure the Experiences in AI Search, AI Search FAQ

Important Limitation
There is no OOB setting to globally say "always rank meta matches above title/content matches." Title/content/meta are all part of the AI Search relevancy model, but the platform does not expose a direct static weight control per field. Therefore, the supported OOB approach is:

Index meta as searchable
Reindex
Use synonyms where needed
Use Result Improvement Rules for targeted boosting/promotion Content Creation for Relevancy in AI Search, Result improvement rules

  • How are scores calculated for AI Search results
    AI Search relies on a variety of content features for the relevancy ranking of search result documents. These include:

Title match — how well the query matches the document's title
Content match — how well the query matches the document's body content
Keyword match — how well the query matches the document's tags or meta
Keyword popularity — the popularity of the document's tags or meta
Document freshness — how recently the document was created and/or updated
Document popularity — how often the document has been viewed

Content Creation for Relevancy in AI Search

main.Subject: Search not working expectedly in Employee Center
main.Description:
Search option is not working consistently or giving results all times when some text parameters are input to look for Catalog items, knowledge articles, etc. It sometimes gives the results but sometimes gives no results. It is not working consistently at all times. 
Please refer from the attached if we type techno for technology request it doesn't make any suggestion.
main.Resolution notes:
[code]

SOLUTION PROPOSED

Hello Eshanand,

CAUSE:

After working with SMEs on this matter it is as I suspected. This behavior is working as expected and suggested results will not show a record if the entered search term is not 1) indexed under that record via a token and 2) a subset of the records title.

When testing during our last meeting I was able to show that the terms "tech" and "technolo" are not indexed search terms (tokens) for the "Technology Request" catalog item.
This is because when the system indexes a record it uses a "stemming" algorithm that looks for a common "root" of a search term. It will then search based on that root. If no root is found, it searches for the string it received and if no tokens match, we will get no results.

After making this findings we can verify that your instance does return results for 3 letter tokens such as "app" since this is a root word for "Application".

Ultimately, the system will only index root words for a record using a stemming algorithm and if your search term is not in that list of tokens you will have to search with the whole word to get search suggestions

SOLUTION:

After additional searching I was able to find that you can manually add your own search terms/tokens for a records that will be added to it's index.

To do this you simply need to go to the catalog item's record in the platform, find the "meta" field, then add your desired search tokens there.

Community Article:
https://www.servicenow.com/community/itsm-forum/adding-quot-tags-quot-or-quot-keywords-quot-to-catalog-items-and/m-p/742323

VERIFICATION:

I tested this with your "Technology Request" catalog item adding the terms "tec" and "technolo".

main.Subject: Employee center pro and facets panel filters inconsistency
main.Description:
Using employee center pro search in our production instance: https://servicemgt.service-now.com/esc
Searching for "Imperial Values" the search page opens with 3 filters (Source, KA, Request categories) - see attached 'filters less'
Clicking on "Articles" in the Sources filter, more filters appear - see attached 'filters more'
Why does this happen and why is the behaviour different to our dev and test instances 'servicemgtdev' and 'servicemgttst'.
main.Resolution notes:
Hello Mushaf,

Thanks for your patience while I was checking with the Ai Search team

AI Search team confirmed this is a default behaviour and working as expected. The filters will enable disable based on data. If you go to next page or select any existing filter it filters the data and based on that data the new filters will show up.

It has been noted in the documentation for a long time:
https://www.servicenow.com/docs/bundle/zurich-platform-administration/page/administer/ai-search/concept/content-security-ais.html

"If AI Search applies late binding security to any results from an indexed source used by a facet, the list of available filter selections for the facet changes. When this happens, the facet only displays field values found in the current page of search results."

Whenever AIS cannot evaluate security with early binding, it will fall back to late binding. The "force late binding" property just forces this behavior, but even when it's off, AIS still always has the option to fall back to late-binding.

 Please feel free to update for any query or concern

Kind Regards,
Vijay

Most Probable Cause:
This behavior is documented in PRB1856273, it is working as expected.

The AIS indexed source for the Requested Item [sc_req_item] table has a field setting with attribute map_to that maps the source field short_description to an AIS index field also named short_description. However, short_description is not a

Indexed Source: Requested Item Table

If a bad map_to setting is confirmed, correct the value to use a valid AIS index field. 

You can either try the below two ways:                                                                                                                          
  - Use short_description_s if the field should be stored as a filterable keyword/string                                                                                                                                                            
  - Use short_description_text if the field should be full-text searchable    

Or else use the standard schema procedure:                                                                                                                                                                      
  - map it to a standard OOB AIS index field such as title or text if that reflects the intended use

main.Resolution notes:
Hello  Sonja,

We are placing this case in a Solution Proposed state as I have identified the root cause and provided the solution

Below is the Root Cause Summary for this event.

Please let me know if you have any questions by updating this case.


ISSUE:  AI Search in csm portal does not return any results for catalog items

ROOT CAUSE: 
Thankyou for your patience while we investigated this issue.

Upon detailed analysis, we identified that the behavior was related to the EVAM View configuration associated with the AI Search Bundle for the CSM/ CSP portal

Specifically:

- The EVAM View Config (CSM Catalog) tied to the AI Search Global / Catalog Item bundle  did not have a View template configuews 
- Due to the absence of a View template the system was able to calculate and display the count, but could not render / display the actual search results

Additionally:
1. The required Navigation declarative action was not linked
2. The table fields and custom fields required for rendering search results were either incomplete or not properly configured.

AI Search internally retrieves matching records and calculates the count. However, without a View Template  and proper field mappings, the UI layer cannot render the result cards/items - resulting in a scenario where only the count is displayed but no visible results appear


Solution Proposed:

To resolve the issue, the following changes were impleemented:
1. Configured the  EVAM View Template 
- Added the appropriate View Template for : the catalog items
> AI Search Global | Catalog Item v2

- Ensured it is correctly mapped under:
> AI Search for Customer Portals

2. Linked Navigation Action:
- Added and linked the existing "navigation" declarative action under:
> Evam View Config Action Assignment
> This ensures proper redirection and interaction with search results

3. Updated Table fields:

- Included relevant fields to be displayed :
> Description, Name, Short Description, ETC

4. Configured the custom fields

5. Validation
- After implementing the above configurations, testing was performed 
- The search results are now displayed correctly along with the count, as expected

main.Resolution notes:
Hi Jamie Kerr,

Thank you so much for raising this — it's a genuinely important question, and the fact that you're thinking carefully about how your pharmacy teams access and engage with content tells us a lot about how seriously you take their experience. That matters, and we want to make sure we give you the best possible path advise.

We've given this a great deal of thought, and we'd love to share what we've found — not to tell you what to do, but because we believe the insight will be just as valuable to you as it has been to us.

---

You mentioned wanting to make articles publicly accessible so your CP customers can reach them more easily. We completely understand the instinct — removing barriers feels like the right thing to do for your customers. And in many cases, it is.

However, in this specific situation, opening the content up publicly would actually work against the very experience you're trying to create for your pharmacies. Here's what we mean:

**Your customers deserve content that speaks directly to them.**
Right now, we use a feature called Knowledge Blocks to make sure that each pharmacy only sees the screenshots, guidance, and information that is relevant to their country and setup. It's one of the things your customers may not even notice — but they benefit from every single time they open an article. If the content becomes public, that personalisation disappears entirely, and every customer would see every variant of every piece of content, regardless of whether it applies to them. The experience becomes noisier, not clearer.

**Your engagement data is one of your most valuable assets.**
Knowing which pharmacies are reading which articles — and which ones aren't — gives you the ability to reach out proactively, spot adoption challenges early, and demonstrate real value to the business. The moment content goes public, that signal disappears into the noise of anonymous traffic. You'd lose the ability to distinguish an engaged pharmacy partner from a casual visitor who landed on the page by accident.

**You're building something bigger here.**
We know the direction of travel is to make ServiceNow the home for your Community Pharmacy customer relationships — onboarding, support, self-service, and beyond. That vision is genuinely exciting, and it's the right one. But it only works if customers are connected to the platform. Freely available content, while well-intentioned, quietly removes one of the most natural reasons for a pharmacy to create an account and stay engaged.

---

So what do we recommend?

Rather than opening the content up, you should concentrate on making the account creation journey as smooth and frictionless as possible for your CP customers. That way, they get easy access to everything they need — and you keep all the benefits that come with a connected, authenticated experience.

You could explore options like streamlined self-registration, email domain validation for pharmacy teams, and tailored User Criteria settings that make the right content immediately visible to the right people from the moment they log in.

You've clearly put a lot of care into this, and we love the fact that you channel that energy into a solution that truly serves your customers. 

Warm regards,
Galimbek Sagidenov
ServiceNow Support

When accessing the Search Application configuration from the portal, an informational message is displayed at the top warning that enabling "Exact Match" may lead to navigation issues, as portals do not support this feature. If you have any questions or need anything else related to this Case, kindly contact us or update the case and we will be happy to assist you further. If this resolves your issue, please consider closing the Case by clicking on "Accept Solution".


REASON FOR SOLUTION PROPOSED:
I have gathered all the relevant information to address your inquiry regarding comparing Zing and AI Search metrics, and have confirmed the current limitations around pre-migration comparison reporting.


ISSUE:
You requested guidance on enabling and configuring AI Search for the Service Portal to replace legacy Zing search, with a specific need for metrics that could be used to compare Zing and AI Search performance — including how those metrics are defined, calculated, and tracked — in order to justify the transition to leadership.


INFORMATION:

Official Comparison Statistics:
After consulting with our internal Product and Development teams, I can confirm that there are no official comparison statistics or native reports available that pull data from both Zing and AI Search simultaneously. Because the two engines are fundamentally different in how they operate, ServiceNow does not provide a built-in "side-by-side" comparison report for the two platforms.

AI Search Analytics Dashboard:
Once AI Search is enabled and actively used, the built-in Analytics Dashboard provides the following metrics that can support a before-and-after evaluation:

  • Self-Solved Rate – Successful searches resulting in user clicks
  • Queries with No Results – Zero-result search volume
  • Queries with No Clicks – Searches returning results but with no user engagement
  • Average Click Position – How quickly users find relevant results
  • Average Response Time – Search performance speed
  • Search Users and Total Query Volume – Usage trends over time

These metrics are valuable for demonstrating search relevance, result quality, and user engagement improvements after migration. However, they require AI Search to be enabled and generating usage data before they become available.

Reference: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/ai-search/ai-search-analytics-dashboard.html

Recommended Approach for Leadership Sign-Off:
Rather than a direct data comparison (which is not natively supported), we recommend a Proof of Value approach in a sub-production environment:

  1. Enable AI Search in a sub-prod instance
  2. Use the AI Search Analytics Dashboard to demonstrate reduction in zero-result queries compared to known Zing pain points
  3. Showcase Natural Language Understanding (NLU) and typo tolerance — capabilities Zing does not support
  4. Use this data to build a leadership-facing business case

Key Differences Between Zing and AI Search:

CapabilityZingAI Search
Search MethodExact keyword matchingIntent-based / NLU
Typo ToleranceLimitedNative
Synonym HandlingLimitedNative
Personalized ResultsNoYes (role, dept, location)
Analytics DashboardNoYes
Now Assist / GenAI ReadyNoYes (prerequisite)

Reporting Differences:
Zing metrics are captured in legacy logs, while AI Search uses the Advanced AI Search Management Tools and its own analytics dashboard. These are separate systems with no unified reporting layer between them.

Reference: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/release-notes/advanced-ais-mgmt-tools-rn.html?contentId=HiHtqw9P0yQMS7COmsdo~w

Migration Resources:

  • AI Search Overview: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/platform-administration/ai-search/overview-ais.html
  • Migration Guide (Zing to AIS): https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/platform-administration/ai-search/migrate-srch-apps-ais-next-exp.html?contentId=a1bSCrmEmt95ZRrnObFdvw
  • Zing vs AI Search Community Article: https://www.servicenowzone.com/zing-vs-ai-search-in-servicenow.php

NEXT STEPS:

  1. Review the AI Search Analytics Dashboard documentation linked above to familiarize your team with the available post-migration metrics.
  2. Consider enabling AI Search in a sub-prod environment to begin generating baseline analytics data using the Proof of Value approach outlined above.
  3. Use those sub-prod metrics to build your leadership comparison narrative prior to production rollout.
  4. If you have any additional questions or need clarification on any of the above, please update the case and I will be happy to assist.

main.Resolution notes:
Hi Karthik, 

Thank you for providing the updated steps to reproduce the issue.

I've received feedback from our development team regarding the custom matchers for email fields. Unfortunately, due to the Email field type constraints, standard custom matchers won't work directly. However, there is a workaround available, though it does require several configuration steps:

1. **Create a mirrored String field** to duplicate your Email field data and create a database index for this new field (required for custom matcher functionality)

2. **Write a script** to populate this String field with values from your existing Email field

3. **Create a Business Rule** to maintain the relationship between the fields - whenever the email field is inserted or updated, the String field updates automatically

4. **Duplicate your existing matcher** and modify it to reference the new String field instead of the Email field

5. **Configure matchers** for your specific search application

While this approach is more complex than a direct solution, it will allow you to achieve the custom matching functionality you need for email fields.

I'll place the case in Solution Proposed while you review the workaround approach. This does not close the case automatically. If you have questions about implementing any of these steps or need additional guidance, just update the case and I'll assist you further.

main.Subject: Service Portal 検索欄からの検索について
main.Description:
Service Portal の検索欄からナレッジ記事を検索する際の仕様についてご教授いただけますでしょうか。

【背景】
1. 添付画像1 のような Service Portal の検索欄を用いて、ナレッジ記事の検索を行い、記事が正しく検索されるかを確認しています。
2. 検索対象となるナレッジ記事は、ナレッジカテゴリから表示されていることを確認しています。
　- 該当記事が公開済みかつアクティブ
　- 該当記事を登録したナレッジベースは、新規で別途作成したナレッジベース
3. Service Portal 検索欄にキーワードを入力し、検索を行うと添付画像2 のナレッジ記事が検索されませんでした。

つきまして、下記についてご質問させていただきたく存じます。

1. Service Portal の検索欄で検索を行う際に、何の対象（ソース）を検索し、その結果を返すのでしょうか。

2. Service Portal の構成画面にて、AI Search が既定でオンになっており、Service Portal Default Search Application が指定されています。
この場合、Service Portal の検索欄は AI Search を使用して検索を行い、その結果を返す認識が正しいでしょうか。
認識齟齬がある場合、Service Portal の検索欄が使用する Application, Search Engine をお教えいただけますでしょうか。

3. 質問2の想定を前提にしたご質問となります。
Service Portal Default Search Application の Search Profile に、Service Portal Default Search Profile が既定で設定されており、
Search Source が以下になっていることから、これらをソースにして検索結果を表示しているのではないかと推察しました。
・Service Portal Knowledge Bases
・Service Portal Catalogs

Service Portal Knowledge Bases の検索条件では、既定でOOTBで作成済みのナレッジベースが指定されている認識ですが、
該当箇所の設定により、添付画像3 のような確認結果が得られた認識で正しいでしょうか。
前提が間違っている場合、質問2での正しい Application, Search Engine に加え、Service Portal の検索欄が使用する検索ソースをご回答いただけますと幸いです。

4. Service Portal の検索欄と、タスクレコード（インシデントや問題、変更等）のフォーム上に表示できる「Related Search Results」の検索は、異なる機能でしょうか。仕様の違いをお教えいただけますでしょうか。
例）検索時の Search Engine や Source が異なる　など

5. Service Portal の検索欄からキーワードを入力する際に、キーワードを完全一致させる必要がございますでしょうか。
例）「VPN設定」の検索結果を表示したい場合、「VPN」のみをキーワードにすると検索されないことは仕様　など

以上、よろしくお願いいたします。

main.Subject: Self-Solved Rate metric in AI Search Analytics
main.Description:
I have two questions related to AI Search Analytics:
1. I understand the "Self-Solved Rate" calculates which searches lead to a "click". The higher the percentage, the higher "success" is for them finding something without having to submit a case. However, what if they search and then "click" on the appropriate catalog item/form that shows up in the search? Does that count towards this? Or what is the filter condition for this metric - only if they click Knowledge Articles and not catalog items?

2. What does "***" mean when it shows it as a top query?
main.Resolution notes: Hello Eun, We are placing this into Solution Proposed as we believe the information provided below will resolve your issue. If you have any questions or need anything else related to this Case, Kindly contact us or update the case and we will be happy to assist you further. If this resolves your issue, please consider closing the Case by clicking on "Accept Solution". AFFECTED INSTANCES: Production / Sub-production (as applicable) ISSUE: You are seeking clarification on two AI Search Analytics behaviors: 1. Whether the **Self-Solved Rate** metric only includes clicks on Knowledge Articles or also includes other result types such as catalog items, forms, and other searchable records. 2. What the value "***" represents when it appears in the Top Queries section of AI Search Analytics. SOLUTION PROPOSED: Thank you for your patience and for the opportunity to assist you with this matter. Throughout my investigation, I paid close attention to your specific needs, and I noticed uncertainty around how search result interactions are classified within AI Search Analytics and how certain query values are represented in reporting. This insight allowed me to tailor a solution that not only addresses your requirements but also supports a seamless and positive experience for you and your team. I'm confident that this approach will resolve your concerns and provide the results you're looking for. Please find the details of my proposed solution below: 1. **Self-Solved Rate behavior** * The Self-Solved Rate is defined as the percentage of search queries that result in a search result click (selection). * Based on the documentation, this metric is not limited to Knowledge Articles only. * Any clickable result returned by the configured AI Search application (such as Knowledge Articles, catalog items, forms, or other indexed records) may contribute to this metric, as long as the user selects a result from the search results page. * The dashboard does not provide a breakdown by content type, so all supported result types are aggregated in this metric. https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/platform-administration/ai-search/ai-search-dashboard.html?contentId=SGS5F9jcd5NIPZn9txhoRw 2. **Meaning of "***" in Top Queries** * "***" represents a non-specific or generalized search entry captured by the analytics system. * It indicates cases where the original query text is not explicitly stored or is aggregated at a system level. * This typically reflects broad or normalized search behavior rather than a literal user-entered keyword. * As such, "***" should be interpreted as an aggregated search placeholder rather than a direct query string. 3. **Reporting limitation note** * AI Search Analytics does not provide further granularity on Self-Solved Rate by result type or detailed decoding of aggregated query placeholders. * For deeper analysis, review of raw search events may be required via the underlying search event tables. main.Subject: AI Search - Similar queries not returning the same search results
main.Description:
Hello team,

I am an admin user. And I have noticed that on the Service Portal, similar queries are returning different search results.

Examples - 

1] "I need corporate card" and "corporate card"
2] "copilot", "co-pilot", "co pilot", "MS co-pilot", "Microsoft co-pilot", "MS co pilot", "Microsoft co pilot".

In both of the above cases, the intent of the search query is same and we would expect AI search to show similar results ( At least the first page ). However same is not the case. 

PFA screenshots for more details.

We have already tried manually indexing the tables. Didn't work.
main.Resolution notes:
Hi Swati,

Thank you for your follow-up and for taking the time to share your concerns. Your question about scalability is completely valid, and I want to address it directly.

To set clear expectations: AI Search does not have a built-in mechanism to automatically detect and group semantically similar queries without some degree of initial configuration. This is working as designed and I appreciate your understanding of this matter.

AI Search uses a combination of vector-based semantic matching and indexed keyword relevance to surface results. However, it does not automatically infer intent variations (e.g., "I need a corporate card" → catalog item "Corporate Card Request") or resolve spelling/phrasing variations (e.g., "co-pilot" vs "copilot") without being explicitly told how those terms relate to one another.

The two supported tools for addressing this are:
Synonyms — for phrasing/spelling variants of the same concept (your "copilot" scenario). Once created, these persist and continue to work for any new content automatically — so this is a one-time setup per concept, not per-item maintenance. ServiceNow does provide an out-of-the-box base synonym dictionary as a starting point; however, this dictionary is a general reference and is not tailored or maintained on a per-customer basis. Maintaining and expanding the synonym list to reflect your organization's specific terminology and use cases is the responsibility of your team.
Promote rules (Result Improvement Rules) — for pinning specific documents or catalog items to appear for a given query. This is intentional curation, not a workaround.

Scalability concern:
For the "corporate card" scenario specifically, the Promote rule does require you to be aware of new catalog items and manually add them. However, a practical way to reduce this overhead would be to:
1. Review your AI Search query logs periodically to identify high-volume queries with poor results, and address them in batches.
2. Build out your synonym dictionary now for known variant terms — once a synonym group exists, any new content indexed under those terms will benefit from it automatically.

Is there an alternative?
The Now Assist for AI Search product does offer more intelligent, AI-driven query understanding that can reduce the need for manual curation. I would recommend reaching out to your ServiceNow Solution Consultant, Enrico Reggi, to discuss whether that product is a fit for your needs.

To summarize: what you are experiencing is expected behaviour in standard AI Search, and the current configuration I applied is the supported resolution path. I appreciate that it requires some ongoing awareness, but it is not as intensive as it may seem once the initial synonym and rule configuration is in place.

Please let me know if you have any further questions.

Thanks and kind regards,
Drew

Hello Mayra,

We are placing this case in a Solution Proposed state as the issue has been resolved in both your production and sandbox environments, and all outstanding RCA questions have been addressed.

Below is the Root Cause Summary for this event.

START TIME: 2026-04-21 17:34 (UTC) / 2026-04-21 10:34 (PDT)
END TIME: 2026-04-22 21:28 (UTC) / 2026-04-22 14:28 (PDT)

AFFECTED INSTANCES: rockwellautomation, rockwellautomationsandbox

ISSUE: On April 21, at 14:49 (UTC) / 07:49 (PDT), Rockwell Automation opened CS9172633 to report that AI Search had been unexpectedly enabled on their production instance (rockwellautomation), causing the custom /rocket Service Portal search to return no results when AI Search was disabled for that portal.

IMPACT:
- All users accessing the /rocket Service Portal were unable to retrieve search results when attempting to disable AI Search, as the Rocket Search Application was still pointing to AI Search as its engine.
- You were unable to return search functionality to its previous Zing-based behavior without intervention from ServiceNow.
- Both the production instance (rockwellautomation) and sandbox instance (rockwellautomationsandbox) were affected.

RELIEF PROVIDED:
- We investigated and identified that the Rocket Search Application's search engine configuration was still set to AI Search even after the portal-level AI Search toggle was disabled, causing the complete loss of search results.
- On the production instance, the customer resolved the issue independently by duplicating a record on the sp_ai_search_results_action_config table. ServiceNow's development team confirmed this is an acceptable and sustainable fix.
- On rockwellautomationsandbox, ServiceNow engineers ran a full AI Search disable script (deleteAllAisConnections, setAisEventQueueWritable false, setAisServerWritable false, disableAis) and removed the AISearch record from the sys_service table. AI Search was subsequently reprovisioned on sandbox via CHG72900609 so the customer could complete their planned Zing-to-AIS migration and validate the configuration.

ROOT CAUSE:
- AI Search was provisioned on the instance without customer initiation. A sys_service record named "AISearch" was originally created in 2023 when AI Search was first provisioned on the instance. On 2026-04-16, something triggered the RequestAIS process in Glide (navigating to All > AI Search > AI Search Status > Request AI Search), which caused the instance to automatically ping the datacenter. The DISH service then reprovisioned AI Search via DishMainScheduledJob, resulting in CHG72699195 being executed by datacenterautomation@snc.maint.
- The exact user or automated process that clicked the Request AI Search button on 2026-04-16 could not be confirmed from available logs. 
- Once AI Search was active, the Rocket Search Application's engine defaulted to AI Search. Disabling AI Search at the portal level without explicitly reconfiguring the search engine caused all search results to stop returning.

On behalf of ServiceNow, we apologize for the impact this issue has had on your organization. Our number one priority is your successful use of ServiceNow. We want to provide you with the support you deserve. If you have any further questions or concerns, please update this case.

main.Subject: Influx of ais_index events observed
main.Description: Customer observed influx of ais_index events and want to understand the cause of it. can you please review and provide an update to the customer. Customer updated as part of CS9171554
main.Resolution notes:
[code]

Hello Ahamadunnisa,

I hope you are doing well. Thank you for your continued collaboration.

By design, AI Search indexes all fields on records within any table configured as an Indexed Source (ais_datasource). For each indexed source, AI Search incrementally processes record changes by generating a sys_event entry in the AIS index queue. These events are triggered by every INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE action on the record and are processed by a single AIS Index Event Processor (sys_trigger), which runs every 30 seconds. This approach helps ensure that any updates to records are promptly reflected in AI Search results.

In this case, I am observing a high volume of updates occurring on the sys_user_group table. As a result, indexing events are being generated for fields such as sys_mod_count, sys_updated_by, and sys_updated_on. Since these fields are not typically used for AI Search queries, it would be safe to mark them as no_text_index. This configuration will prevent indexing events from being triggered when updates occur on the sys_user_group table and will help reduce the number of records generated in the sysevent table for processing.

At this time, updates to the sys_user_group table alone are responsible for generating approximately 235,509 indexing events in the sysevent table.

You can update the configuration directly from the indexed source record for sys_user_group by navigating to the Field Settings & Mapping related list using the following link:

  • https://amadeus.service-now.com/nav_to.do?uri=ais_datasource.do?sys_id=44be42b477033010346b53892c5a99ed

Please ensure that no_text_index is set to true for the relevant fields so searchable content indexing is disabled for those fields.

For additional details and best practices, I recommend reviewing the following documentation, which provides further guidance on this topic:

  • https://support.servicenow.com/kb?id=kb_article_view&sysparm_article=KB1644352
  • https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/ai-search/field-settings-ais.html?section=field-settings-ais

If you have any questions or would like assistance reviewing or validating these configuration changes, please don't hesitate to let me know. I'll be happy to support you further.

Best regards,
Keylor Steven Villarreal Baltodano
Senior Technical Support Engineer – Platform Tech
📅 Monday to Friday | 🕕 9:00 AM – 6:00 PM (US MDT)

main.Resolution notes: Hello Martin, We are placing this case in a Solution Proposed state as the root cause of the ais_index event queue spike has been fully identified, a known product defect has been confirmed, and a fix is in the way to be release in June. [code]Affected Instances:[/code] citigroupitsm (Production) [code]Issue:[/code] On April 22nd, 2026, the production instance experienced a severe spike of over 1.5 million [code]ais_index[/code] events within a two-hour window, causing a significant backlog in the event queue and temporarily delaying event processing. [code]Solution Proposed:[/code] ServiceNow engineers investigated and identified the following root cause: The Zurich P5HF1 to P6HF2 upgrade applied on April 20th introduced the AI Search Indexed Source for [code]sam_sw_product_lifecycle[/code] for the first time as part of the Content Library Portal feature. When the OOTB SAM scheduled job [code]"Download Software Content: Product Lifecycles"[/code] ran for the first time post-upgrade on April 22nd, the AIS indexing engine had no prior baseline for this table and generated index events for all 1.5+ million existing records simultaneously, overwhelming the AIS Index Event Processor. This behavior is attributed to a known product defect [code]PRB2010143[/code], which identifies that the AI Search indexed source for [code]sam_sw_product_lifecycle[/code] was not configured with the [code]no_text_index[/code] attribute for system fields that do not require indexing. ServiceNow provided an interim fix update set (attached to this case) containing the [code]no_text_index[/code] attribute configuration for all relevant fields on the [code]sam_sw_product_lifecycle[/code] indexed source. Your team has already applied the [code]no_text_index[/code] attribute to the following fields on the production instance: [code]- sys_mod_count[/code] [code]- sys_updated_by[/code] [code]- sys_updated_on[/code] [code]- lifecycle_type[/code] [code]Next Steps:[/code] 1. The update set covers a broader set of fields than those applied manually and includes the [code]replace on upgrade[/code] option, ensuring a clean transition when the permanent fix is released. 2. [code]Monitor the ais_index queue:[/code] After applying the full update set, monitor [code]ais_index_queue_stats[/code] following the next scheduled run of [code]"Download Software Content: Product Lifecycles"[/code] to confirm that event volumes remain within normal levels. 3. Once available on the ServiceNow Store, we recommend updating the Content Library Portal application to apply the OOB fix. Please let me know if you have any questions by updating this case. main.Resolution notes:
[code]

Hello Sree Vatsava,

Thanks for joining the call.

We are moving the case to Solution Proposed.
Below are the details of our investigation on your case. Please feel free to update the case for any queries, and we would be happy to address them!

Issue:
Knowledge Article and community Posts search using AI Search from Portal

Investigation Details:

1) Query regarding the warning message at the top of OOTB record:

The warning banner is the standard ServiceNow "customized OOTB record" notification. It appears whenever you modify a record that was originally shipped by ServiceNow (OOTB) specifically to alert that the platform's default definition for that record may change in a future release or upgrade.
The warning is informational only. It does not mean the customization will be automatically overwritten. By default, when you customize an OOTB record in ServiceNow, the "Replace on upgrade" flag on the record is set to false in sys_update_xml. With this flag set to false, the upgrade process will skip that record and preserve the customer's customization. The customization is safe to keep.

-> The scenario where a customization could be overwritten is if the "Replace on upgrade" is set as true on the record — in that case, the next upgrade would restore the OOTB default and the customization would be lost. The customer should verify that the "Replace on upgrade" flag is not set to true on their customized search source record.

-> You could also follow the process of making a copy of the same Search Source and modify the new one instead of the OOTB one, and use that instead.

2) Does AI Search supports searching Community Posts Search:

Since you have a table configured in your instance specific to Community posts, you can definitely use that and create a new Indexed Source, Map that Indexed Source to a Search Source, which in turn is to be mapped to a Search Profile and Search Application. Make sure to re-index the Indexed Source, and test.
In case you face any issues with EVAM configurations or Search results for community posts, as discussed on call, kindly raise a separate case for it to be investigated.
