main.Subject: Virtual Agent provides wrong information issue for Tech Hub request
main.Description:
The question in Virtual agent is “find me the closest tech hub”.

We impersonated as “Todd fox” in dev1, and got below different answers. For the second screenshot, we don’t even know where VA found the 2400” as we can’t find it anywhere from the KBs listed in “show sources” at the end of the results.

Here’s the KBs listed in “show sources”:
https://dowdev1.service-now.com/esc?id=kb_article&sys_id=8fc8ba6c8716ae103566fcc6cebb354c
https://dowdev1.service-now.com/esc?id=kb_article&sys_id=1f3cfa9797f03650d7b27e200153af21

Also, we noticed that sometimes there’s no “show sources” button at all, is it expected? When will we have “show sources” and when not?
main.Resolution notes:
[code]

Hey Team

Thank you for your patence as we worked to resolve this issue.

Issue Summary

After mapping the location field to cmn_location on the sys_user AI datasource and re-indexed you confirmed that NAVA still returns the wrong tech hub. The datasource fix did not resolve the inconsistent/incorrect location recommendation. This confirms the root cause is not missing field indexing — it is how AI Search retrieves and ranks the grounding documents that NAVA's LLM then picks from.


What is happening

First, the search engine matches semantically, not logically. The query's top-matching documents get returned as the top result and then get picked by the LLM. The LLM doesn't compute "closest" — it picks from whatever AI Search ranked highest. If multiple tech hub KB articles are semantically similar to "find me the closest tech hub," the ranking can vary between runs, which produces exactly the inconsistency that we see in this case

Second, the documented remedy is a Result Improvement Rule (RIR) to deterministically promote the correct document when trigger terms match, rather than relying on the field mapping alone. Using a Result Improvement Rule to promote the document guarantees the item is returned in the top results when triggers match, so the LLM can then pick it.

Critical architecture point : Because you are using Enhanced Chat, Portal and NAVA are tied to the same search profile, so any item restricted or promoted affects both Portal Search and NAVA. This means RIR changes are testable through Portal search before validating in NAVA.


Root Cause / Explanation

The location field mapping was necessary but insufficient. The real failure is in retrieval ranking. "Find me the closest tech hub" is a semantic query against a set of tech hub KB articles. With no deterministic ranking signal tying the user's specific location to the correct article, AI Search returns whichever article is most textually similar — and the LLM picks from that top set. The user's location.name being present in the profile payload helps only if the KB content and the ranking actually surface the matching hub article to the top. Since several Dow sites and hubs appear across the KBs, the semantic match is ambiguous, producing inconsistent answers.

This is why re-indexing the location field changed nothing: indexing made the field available, but did not change which document ranks first for an ambiguous query.


Recommended Resolution

Step 1 — Create Result Improvement Rules for each tech hub (primary fix)

Create an RIR that promotes that hub's KB article when the query contains both location-identifying terms and "tech hub." Navigate to AI Search → Result Improvement Rules.

Configure triggers so that, for example, a query containing "tech hub" combined with a Freeport/Texas signal promotes the Texas hub article to the top. Reference: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/ai-search/create-result-improve-rule-ais.html,
https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/ai-search/result-improvement-rules-ais.html

Step 2 — Confirm the search source returns the user's location as a ranking signal

The search source 9c88954f53171010069addeeff7b1220 must surface location.name so it can participate in matching. The field mapping James added is the prerequisite; verify it is now actually returned in search results by running an AI Search preview for a test user.

Now assist in virtual agent does show the location verified in search preview

Step 3 — Validate via Portal search first (Enhanced Chat shortcut)

Because Dow uses Enhanced Chat, Portal and NAVA share the search profile. Test your RIR by running the query in Portal AI Search as the impersonated user (Jesse Ringel, Donald Wright). If Portal returns the correct hub deterministically, NAVA will too. This is faster than spinning up VA conversations for each test.

Step 4 — Verify in sys_generative_ai_log

After the RIR is active, run a NAVA conversation and inspect the log. The promoted hub article should now appear at the top of the retrieved grounding documents, and the LLM's answer should consistently name the correct hub.

Step 5 — Recommended approach for consistent results: use a deterministic VA topic

For a query like "find me the closest tech hub," the most reliable path to consistent answers is a deterministic VA topic rather than generative retrieval. Instead of letting the LLM pick from semantically ranked search results — which is inherently variable — a scripted topic reads the user's location reference field directly and looks up the mapped tech hub through a defined table relationship. This guarantees the same input always produces the same output, which is exactly what Dow is asking for.

The two approaches serve different goals, and it's worth being explicit with the customer about the trade-off: Result Improvement Rules (Steps 1–4) make the generative path more reliable, but it remains best-effort because the LLM is still selecting from ranked candidates. A deterministic topic removes that variability entirely by resolving location to hub through logic, not language matching. Given that the core complaint is inconsistency, the deterministic topic is the stronger long-term solution, with RIR as the faster interim improvement while the topic is built.

Next Steps:

Please do not reject the solution if you have additional question, the case remains open until you except the solution of the case is closed. Please let me know if you have any additional questions or concerns, If needed we can schedule a zoom meeting. I am available from 8:30am - 4:30pm EST on weekdays.

If you do not have any additional questions please feel free to accept the solution to close the case, at your earliest convenience.

It was a pleasure to serve you.

Have a Great Day on purpose!

ServiceNow
James Darden
Sr Tech Support Engineer
P: 321 251 2286

[/code]

main.Subject: Keyword Search in AI Search is not working as expected on Employee Center Portal
main.Description:
Hello Team,

We currently have keyword search enabled on our employee center portal, which displays knowledge articles when users search through the AI search feature. Currently the AI Search returns articles if the keywords entered by the user are found in the knowledge article's short description, content, or metadata, which we feel like is not the ideal behavior.

We would like the keyword search to return articles based only on the knowledge article metadata, without considering the article short description or content. This way we will be able to have relevant articles appear when user search through AI Search.

Best Regards,
Hemant Langar
main.Resolution notes:
Thanks Hemant for meeting with us earlier today,

We are placing this case in a Solution Proposed state and will include a summary of your case details for our records. 

ISSUE: 

Keyword Search in AI Search is not working as expected on Employee Center Portal

SOLUTION PROPOSED: 

The details on how to change the search to AND and not OR can be found in the following docs in which you can adjust the glide.ais.query.search_operator

https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/washingtondc/platform-administration/ai-search/system-properties-ais.html

In the docs above search for the glide.ais.query.search_operator property and it will provide the details on what values are available. 

To restrict the AI Search search only specific fields and leave out others you can add the no_text_index attribute to the fields you do not want searchable by AI Search. 

The following article provides more details:

https://support.servicenow.com/kb?id=kb_article_view&sys_kb_id=2442542d97f1ee5068d477121153af37

NEXT STEPS: 

Please let us know if you need any further clarification on the information shared and we will be happy to help.

main.Subject: Global search not working with AI Search
main.Description:
Hi team,

Context:
We recently installed the "Now Assist for IT Service Management (ITSM)" on our instance and we are configuring it.

We configured the AI Search for Next Experience using "Guided Setup for Zing to AI Search Migration" and migrate all of our search configuration using Zing for Ai Search.
The Search Application "AI Search For Next Experience" was created.
The Search Profile "Next Experience Search Configuration" was created.

When an admin do a global search with an incident number and click on "view all results for ..." it displays a list of results and the record have the short descriptions with the clickable links.
1- When a user that is not admin do the same, he does not have the short description with clickable link on the record so he can see the list of result but cannot open a specific one on another tab (see screenshot 1).

2- When a user that is not admin search by the description of an incident, like "test test", he sometimes has the list of incidents with short description with link on the short description(see screenshot 2).

3- When a user that is not admin search for a change with the change number, has the list with short description links (see screenshot 3).

4- When a user that is not admin search with the incident number, wait for the display of the list and click on the left panel Filters > Source > Incidents, he has the short description and the link (see screenshot 4).

Thanks in advance for your help,

Theo Moreto
main.Resolution notes:
Hi Theo,

I can understand your apprehension related to this resolution, since the behavior seen has changed during a time with no direct changes being made by ServiceNow or your team. In relation to AI Search Source reindexing, however, this behavior is not out of the ordinary.

During indexing, it is expected that there may be a difference in behavior, and at times regression of previously working searches. This is due to the index being rebuilt from scratch, which will take some time to complete depending on the size of the sources.

In addition, the behavior seen by your team can also be attributed to session/caching, which can cause the old index to be used for certain users until their cache is refreshed or the session is re-established. This will happen naturally over time just like the new index's completion, but can make it seem as if the issue is still present until the session/cache catches up to the recent change.

Please do let me know if this explanation helps to explain the resolution we have applied here.
Reference: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/zurich/platform-administration/ai-search/index-single-source-ais.html

At this time, since the original issues presented in this case with your Incident searches are all resolved, I would like to kindly request that the new issues seen with Configuration Items would be handled in a new ticket. With your consent, I would be happy to create this on your team's behalf to allow us to begin investigating this behavior.

Best regards,
Jacob Pinchook | Technical Support Engineer
8am EST - 5pm EST | Monday - Friday

main.Subject: Add a field to Field mapping & settings in AI Search
main.Description: The user needs to add an additional field to the Field mapping & settings section related to AI Search. No further details about the specific field or the context of the change have been provided.
main.Resolution notes:
[code]

Hello Sergio,

Apologies for the delayed answer.

Thank you very much for your time on the previous zoom session, please find a summary of our conversation below.


Core Issue
You created a custom field called "AI description" (an 8K string field) on the ServiceNow catalog item table (sc_cat_item). The field is meant to hold enriched text — business definitions, example queries, and natural language phrases — to help AI Search surface catalog items and record producers when users search with non-exact, conversational language rather than exact names.

What Was Working
The configuration was successfully applied on the record producer (child) table, and testing in the dev environment confirmed it worked — items were found using natural language queries that wouldn't have matched otherwise. In QA (without the configuration), the same queries returned no results.

The Issue
You wanted to apply the same field mapping to the parent catalog item table (sc_cat_item) so that all catalog item types (not just record producers) would benefit. However, when attempting to create a field settings mapping record for sc_cat_item, he received an "Invalid insert" error — because the ai_search_teaser_text map-to value was already mapped for sc_cat_item (as noted in the chat: 'ai_search_teaser_text' already mapped for sc_cat_item). The platform appears to allow this value to be assigned to only one field per index source.

What Was Explored
I have reviewed the index source, confirmed the field was indexed, and walked through the field settings and mappings. He confirmed that ai_search_teaser_text can only be assigned to one field at a time within a given index source. Your underlying goal — having a specific keyword in the custom field return the catalog item in search results — doesn't strictly require that particular map-to value; any valid mapping that gets the field indexed could work.

Further to the summary.

We are placing this issue in Solution Proposed.

Reason:
Cause identified and explained. Resolution provided.

Issue:
Add a field to Field mapping & settings in AI Search

Most Probable Cause:
Certain attributes (like ai_search_teaser_text) can only be added once to an AI Search Indexed Source.

However, once you define an indexed source, AI Search begins automatically indexing to reflect changes to records in the selected source table and its specified child tables.

Solution Proposed:
As per Indexing content from AI Search indexed sources product documentation:

AI Search indexes records on indexed source tables to make their content searchable.

Once you define an indexed source, AI Search begins automatically indexing to reflect changes to records in the selected source table and its specified child tables. The results of all record create, update, and delete operations in these tables are reflected in the search index. AI Search doesn't index content from unmodified records in these tables until you perform a full table index.

When the sc_cat_item.u_ai_description field was created; it inherited the indexing behavior because it belongs to the Catalog Item Table indexed source. As a result, the system began generating AI Search indexes for this field.

Because the field is already included in the indexed source, no additional configuration is required in the Field Settings & Mappings related list. You should be able to retrieve AI Search results when querying based on the sc_cat_item.u_ai_description field.

Please note that certain attribute values —such as ai_search_teaser_text— can only be used once within a single indexed source. However, as mentioned earlier, it is not required to use the ai_search_teaser_text attribute for a field to be available for AI Search query within a particular indexed source.

Please let me know if you need further assistance. I am happy to explain the details on a screen share session.

Thanks.

However, if there are other events already queued ahead of it, the text index event has to wait its turn. This will help speeding up the text_index events processing. To disable text indexing for a table: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/bundle/yokohama-platform-administration/page/administer/search-administration/task/t_RemoveAnIndex.html To disable text indexing for a specific table column: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/bundle/yokohama-platform-administration/page/administer/search-administration/task/t_RemoveAnIndexForASpecificField.html Also, for more details about text indexing, please refer to: KB0721202 - Reduce unnecessary text index events from causing overhead on events processing [code]KB0721202 - Reduce unnecessary text index events from causing overhead on events processing[/code] - Perma Link [public] KB0859922 - Text Indexing - Recommended Field types to set to no_text_index=true [code]KB0859922 - Text Indexing - Recommended Field types to set to no_text_index=true[/code] - Perma Link [public] This KB will help identify which fields are less likely to be useful in text search (text index). main.Subject: Self-Solved Rate for AI Search Analytics dashboard
main.Description: Hi team, I have a question regarding the Self-Solved Rate metric on the AI Search Analytics  dashboard. Could you clarify how exactly this metric is calculated in practice and what is the formula behind it? From the documentation, I understand that it represents % of search queries that resulted in a search result click, and that the chart shows the distribution of queries with and without clicks, along with a trend over the selected time range. I just want to make sure I fully understand what is included in the calculation (e.g. how genius results are counted and if there are any edge cases or exclusions).
main.Resolution notes:
Hello Patrycja Zajac, My name is Galimbek Sagidenov and I am TSE who has been assigned to assist with this case during EMEA hours. We are moving your case to Solution Proposed as we believe the information provided below will resolve your issue. [code]Issue: [/code] You are asking for a detailed explanation of how the Self-Solved Rate metric is calculated in the AI Search Analytics dashboard, specifically how Genius Results are counted and whether any edge cases or exclusions apply to the formula. [code]Business Impact: [/code] Low [code]Investigation Summary: [/code] - Reviewed community article : https://www.servicenow.com/community/intelligence-ml-articles/ai-search-tuning-making-ai-search-analytics-actionable/ta-p/2568580 - Reviewed Product Documentation for Search Signal Tables : https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/platform-administration/search-administration/search-signal-tables.html [code]Solution Proposed: [/code] Thank you for your detailed question — this is a great one to unpack, and I want to make sure you have a complete and accurate picture rather than just a surface-level answer. > What the Self-Solved Rate actually measures The Self-Solved Rate measures how frequently users click on a result in the result list. More precisely, it indicates the percentage of search queries that produced a search result click for the selected application and date range. Under the hood, this is a click-through rate — the date range used in the calculation is not a fixed window; it is defined by the range selector at the top of the dashboard. > Formula (in plain terms) Self-Solved Rate = (Queries where at least one result was clicked / Total queries) × 100 > How Genius Results factor in — and the important edge case This is the most important nuance to be aware of. When a Genius Result is triggered, because the answer is provided as part of the result, a smaller number of clicks is expected. As a consequence, queries where a Genius Result was surfaced but not clicked will contribute to the "Queries with No Clicks" count — effectively reducing the Self-Solved Rate, even though the user may have received a direct, useful answer inline. Crucially, there is currently no way within the dashboard to differentiate between a Genius Result query (where the user got their answer without clicking) and a query where the user simply abandoned without clicking — both show a click rank of "0" and appear in the "Queries with No Clicks" report. The separate Genius Results Triggered vs. Clicked widget gives you visibility into how often Genius Results were presented and how often they were actually clicked, but it does not isolate those queries out of the Self-Solved Rate calculation. > Is Self-Solved Rate the same as Case Deflection Rate? Not directly. While it can serve as a proxy indicator, a click on a result — including a click on a Record Producer that creates a ticket — still counts positively toward the Self-Solved Rate. The metric confirms that users engaged with a result, but it cannot confirm that they resolved their issue without opening a case. For a true case deflection analysis, the Self-Solved Rate would need to be correlated with case/ticket creation data from your ITSM module. > Benchmark A Self-Solved Rate over 50% is considered very good, though a lower rate does not necessarily indicate poor search quality — it may reflect that dynamic teaser text or Q&A Genius Results are providing the answer the user needs without requiring a click. > Where the data lives (for custom reporting) If you need to build custom reports beyond what the dashboard surfaces, the underlying data is stored in the sys_search_event table, along with the signals tables documented in Search Signal Tables product documentation. This is achieved by a client script - https://amazonotsuat.service-now.com/catalog_script_client.do?sys_id=d92c7db788f126104806459088823625&sysparm_record_target=catalog_script_client&sysparm_record_row=2&sysparm_record_rows=4&sysparm_record_list=scriptCONTAINScommon_issues%5Eactive%3Dtrue%5Evariable_set%3Ddfdd323611016210dc3a4904118385e0%5EORDERBYDESCsys_updated_on -- When user selects a symptom, it gets copied over to "Could you describe the issue?" field that is hidden. If user selects Something Else as symptom, "Could you describe the issue?" becomes visible on the form and KB deflection then happens based on the user's manual input.

In all the subprod instances that we have, the KB articles rightly show up details related to ACME, however, production instance search results do not reflect the same. I would like to understand the root cause behind this.
main.Resolution notes:
Hi Siddharth,

We are placing this case in a Solution Proposed state and will include a summary of your case details for our records. 

ISSUE: 

AI Search results giving different results based on the space between '/'  

SOLUTION PROPOSED: 

We were able to confirm that the described behavior with the tokenization with the symbols is by design. 

As mentioned with the example 'ACME/Isolation' with no spaces between the '/' it is treated as a single token when being analyzed versus when spaces are present like 'ACME / Isolation' where the slash acts a word boundary and the query works as expected. 

The difference lies in how the user query is parsed in the first stage of tokenization.

Tokenizes the conjoined terms ACME, /, and Isolation as a PHRASE that must match in that order. There is special joining logic that considers some punctuation as joiners as we observe with the slash character. 

The decision to join terms to phrases by joiner characters is by design and any changes to this  behavior would need to be reviewed by the product team. 

Moving forward I would suggest creating a submission to our idea portal where our product team will review the submission to consider for future releases linked below

https://support.servicenow.com/ideas

In the meantime the previous suggestions outside of creating the space between special characters would be to create synonyms, use result improvement rules and make updates to record meta tags.  

NEXT STEPS: 

Please let us know if any further clarification is needed and we will help the best we can. 

Otherwise feel free to accept the solution to close out your case if no further assistance is needed. 

Best regards,
Brendan

The issue occurs if Typo Handling is enabled in the Search Application, causing the search term to to be autocorrected. This behavior is expected when the term does not exist in indexed records.

https://www.servicenow.com/docs/bundle/zurich-platform-administration/page/administer/ai-search/concept/typo-handling-ais.html

Exclude the search term from the typo handling dictionary to prevent autocorrection. Refer to the documentation for excluding terms: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/bundle/zurich-platform-administration/page/administer/ai-search/task/exclude-typo-handling-terms-ais.html

OR 

Create a record for the particular search term (e.g., a KB article) and ensure it is indexed to appear in search results.

よろしくお願いいたします。
 
【ご質問】
Service Now上でAI検索をする際に利用する検索エンジンの設定変更は可能と認識しておりますが、デフォルトで利用されているエンジンはZingでしょうか？
Service Now上でAI検索をする際に利用する検索エンジンの変更方法をご教示いただくことは可能でしょうか？
Genius Resultを利用したいのですが、必要な設定やプラグイン等の条件はありますでしょうか？
 
《確認済ステータス》
Now Assistは有効化済
AI検索はアクティブ化済
main.Resolution notes:
サポートのユーガンと申します。
いつもお世話になっております。

[Solution Proposed]
以下に回答いたします。

1> Service Now上でAI検索をする際に利用する検索エンジンの設定変更は可能と認識しておりますが、デフォルトで利用されているエンジンはZingでしょうか？

AI Searchをアクティブ化する前のデフォルト検索エンジンはZingとなります。
AI Searchをアクティブ化後は、Zingに代わり、AI Searchが検索エンジンとして使用されます。                  
                  

2>Service Now上でAI検索をする際に利用する検索エンジンの変更方法をご教示いただくことは可能でしょうか？

・AI Searchをアクティブ化後は、自動でAI Searchが検索エンジンとして使用されますので、AI Searchのアクティブ化以外のご対応は不要です。                 


ご参考：
AI SearchからZingに戻すこともできます。
以下のドキュメントをご参照ください。                    
                                                                                
  - Unified Navigation(Global search) の場合：
https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/zurich/platform-administration/ai-search/revert-zing-unified-nav-search.html                 

  - Service Portal / Employee Center の場合：各ポータルのAI Search設定にてAI Searchを無効化することで、Zingにフォールバックされます。                      
  

3>Genius Resultを利用したいのですが、必要な設定やプラグイン等の条件はありますでしょうか？

Genius Result使用の前提条件は、Now Assist の有効化と、AI Search のアクティブ化です。
条件は満たされておりますので、All > AI Search > Now Assist in AI Search SetupよりGenius Resultを有効化いただけます。
Screenshot 2026-05-07 at 11.04.02.pngをご参照ください。


[ネクストアクション]
以上の内容をもって、本件のステータスを Solution Proposed に移動いたします。

ご不明点やご懸念がございましたらお気軽にお問い合わせください。

問題がないようでしたら Accept Solution を押下し、本件をクローズしていただけますと幸いです。

何卒よろしくお願いいたします。
Motomi Iugan | Technical Support, APJ Delivery Services

main.Subject: Employee Center Pro: Facets with no results displayed when Hybrid Search is enabled
main.Description:
When Hybrid Search is enabled in Employee Center Pro, facets/filters with no matching results are still displayed on the search results page.
Displaying facets/filters that do not return any results may be confusing for users.

Expected Behavior
Only facets with one or more matching search results should be displayed.
main.Resolution notes:
Hello Marta,

Thank you very much for your patience and cooperation while we thoroughly investigated this behavior.

After detailed validation and comparison against an Out-of-the-Box (OOTB) instance, we confirmed that the behavior observed is currently working as designed under Hybrid Search functionality and is consistent with existing platform behavior.

Observed Behavior:

1. When Hybrid Search (Now Assist / AI Search hybrid mode) is disabled or not configured in Employee Center:

* Only facets with matching search results are displayed
* Facets with zero results are hidden

2. When Hybrid Search is enabled through AI Search / Now Assist:

* All configured facets and source buckets are displayed, including facets with zero results
* Facet/tab result counts are not displayed
* Conditional hiding of empty facets is currently not supported

Validation Performed:

To validate this behavior, testing was performed in an OOTB instance and the exact same behavior was successfully reproduced.

Before enabling Hybrid Search:

* Only facets containing matching results were displayed
* Example:

  * Searching for "request" displayed both Request and Articles facets because both contained results
  * Searching for "relocation" displayed only the Request facet because the Articles facet had no matching results

After enabling Hybrid Search:

* All facets became visible regardless of whether results were returned
* Facet/tab counts were no longer displayed

For your reference, I have attached screen recordings demonstrating both scenarios from the OOTB instance.

Additional Product Clarification:

During our internal review, this behavior was also confirmed under PRB2016773.

At present, this behavior is considered expected platform behavior when Hybrid Search is enabled and therefore it was not addressed as a product defect fix under the PRB.

However, we completely understand the concern and the impact this may have from a usability and user experience perspective, especially when facets with zero results continue to appear in the Employee Center search experience.

Because multiple customers have raised similar concerns and enhancement requests regarding facet visibility and tab/result counts under Hybrid Search, the product team is actively aware of this feedback and the requested enhancement is currently being considered for a future platform release.

While we unfortunately do not have an exact ETA or committed release version available at this moment, the enhancement request remains under product consideration due to customer demand and feedback received from customers such as yourself.

We truly appreciate you taking the time to raise this concern and work with us throughout the investigation process. Customer feedback like yours plays a very important role in helping improve the overall platform experience and helping guide future product enhancements.

Official Documentation Reference:

https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/yokohama/platform-administration/ai-search/display-result-counts-ais.html

As documented:

* "Search result counts for facets are not displayed when hybrid search is enabled."
* Hybrid Search changes how facets are rendered and aggregated using AI-based ranking behavior.

Conclusion:

1. The current behavior is expected and aligned with OOTB Hybrid Search functionality
2. There is currently no supported configuration available to hide facets with zero results while Hybrid Search is enabled
3. Any change to this behavior today would require custom UI-level implementation outside standard platform capabilities
4. The requested enhancement is already being tracked internally under PRB2016773 and is being considered for inclusion in a future platform release

Please let me know if you have any additional questions or concerns regarding this behavior. I will be very happy to assist you further.

On behalf of ServiceNow, we sincerely apologize for the inconvenience and impact this behavior may have caused to your users and organization. Our priority is always your successful use of the platform, and we truly appreciate your patience, understanding, and continued cooperation throughout this investigation.

Thank you and Kind Regards,
Karthik Iyer

I'm reaching out to provide you with an update regarding your case.
We are moving the case to a Solution Proposed status. Please note that this does not close the case, you can still reply if you have any questions or concerns, and I will be happy to assist you.

Affected Instance:
bakerdev

Issue Summary:
Development instance is slow.

Actions Taken:
- Reviewed the instance health, which showed all nodes had recently restarted, suggesting a possible Out Of Memory (OOM) event.
- Analyzed thread dumps and heap dumps to investigate the potential OOM. Identified thread 'pool-17-thread-1' as consuming a significant amount of memory (47.47% of heap).
- Correlated the high-memory thread 'pool-17-thread-1' with logs from the time of the issue. Found that this thread is associated with AI Search (AIS) indexing for the 'kb_knowledge' table, with numerous warnings about duplicate embedded documents being dropped during ingestion.
- Investigated the 'AIS Index Event Processor' job logs, which confirmed it was actively processing a large number of events for the 'ais_index' queue and reprocessing events due to a stale check-in.
- Checked the event queue ('sysevent') and found a very large backlog of 893,329 unprocessed events in the 'ais_index' queue, confirming heavy AIS activity.
- Identified that the instance is affected by problem PRB1971388, which is fixed in version Y P 12 HF 12 and above. The customer is currently on YP 12 HF 1.

Proposed Solution:
We have confirmed that you are being impacted by problem PRB1971388, which is fixed in version Y P 12 HF 12 and above.
Your instance is currently on YP 12 HF 1.

We recommend to upgrade the instance to the fix version to avoid this issue from continue happening. Let me know if you have any question

main.Subject: Knowledge articles are boosting based on the user language.
main.Description:
Dear Team,
I hope this email finds you well. I am writing to report two critical issues we've identified with the portal's language configuration functionality that require immediate attention. 
Issue 1: Incorrect Language Priority Display We have discovered that the portal is not displaying languages according to the configured priority settings. Expected Behavior:
When a user's language is set to Spanish and their country is Estonia, the system should display Spanish knowledge articles first (primary language), followed by Russian or English articles in random order (fallback languages)
Current Behavior:
The portal is not following this configured language hierarchy and is displaying content incorrectly
Issue 2: Language Search Results Inconsistency There is an inconsistent behavior when users search for articles within specific language filters. 
Current Problem:
When searching for articles under a specific language, only one language appears in the results initially
Other configured languages only become visible after refreshing the browser tab or the entire window
This creates a poor user experience and may cause users to miss relevant content
Impact:
These issues are affecting user experience and potentially preventing users from accessing relevant knowledge articles in their preferred languages. This could lead to:
Reduced user satisfaction
Missed information due to language barriers
Inconsistent portal behavior across different user sessions
Requested Action:
Could you please investigate these language configuration issues and provide:
Root cause analysis for both problems
Estimated timeline for resolution
Any temporary workarounds we can implement while awaiting the fix
I am available to provide additional details, screenshots, or assist with testing as needed. Please let me know if you require any further information to proceed with the investigation.
Thank you for your prompt attention to these matters.


Thanks,
Sai.
main.Resolution notes:
Hello Saireddy,

We are placing this case into Solution Proposed as we believe we have accurately identified the root cause and the appropriate path forward to resolve your language-boosting issue. We sincerely appreciate your patience and engagement throughout this investigation, and we understand the urgency given the impact to your end users across multiple regions.

**REASON FOR SOLUTION PROPOSED:**

Through our investigation and collaboration with you, we have confirmed that the AI Search backend is functioning correctly and returning Knowledge article results in the proper language order (Spanish articles prioritized for Spanish-language users). The remaining issue is isolated to the Service Portal UI widget layer, which is outside the scope of AI Search and requires UX team expertise. We are consolidating all efforts on case CS9299512 with the UX team to ensure this receives the priority and attention it deserves.

**ISSUE:**

End users in multiple regions selecting Spanish as their language preference are seeing English-language Knowledge articles appearing at the top of search results in the Service Portal, instead of Spanish-language articles being prioritized first. This behavior:
1. Was not present prior to the Xanadu patch 9 release.
2. Does not reproduce in the AI Search Preview interface.
3. Only reproduces in the Service Portal UI.

**ROOT CAUSE:**

The AI Search backend is working as designed—it is returning results in the correct language order (Spanish articles first for Spanish-speaking users). The ranking and ordering issue exists at the Service Portal UI widget layer, which handles the presentation of search results to end users. This is a UI rendering issue, not a backend search algorithm issue.

**RESOLUTION:**

Immediate action (this case): The AI Search core functionality has been validated and confirmed working correctly. Your search profile publication (fd6491cb531710... ) has already improved your configuration.

Next steps for full resolution: Case CS9299512 has been escalated to our UX team, who owns the Service Portal widget layer and can implement the necessary UI corrections. We recommend requesting a **escalation** on that case to reflect the business impact and regional scope of this issue. Given the timeline concerns and the fact that this behavior appeared after Xanadu patch 9, the UX team should be able to investigate whether a regression was introduced and prioritize accordingly.

**ADDITIONAL NOTES:**

1. The AI Search backend is functioning correctly—this has been validated through the Search Preview interface and confirmed in our meeting on June 25th.
2. The customer-published search profile has already been implemented and is contributing to the overall solution.

main.Subject: ais_index event queue
main.Description: Currently, the event queue ais_index has around 689 thousand events with the status ready, and the number is still increasing without decreasing.
main.Resolution notes:
[code]

Hello Kaue,

My name is Justin, the engineer assigned to your case, and I'll be assisting you. I have completed an initial investigation into the AIS Index Event Queue behavior reported on your instance and I am sharing my findings together with the recommended actions to address the root cause.

Issue:
The ais_index event queue on the production instance is steadily growing, with the latest snapshot showing approximately 1.28 million events in ready/queued state. The AIS Index Event Processor is actively processing events (~500–1,500 events per 5-minute window), however the rate at which new indexing events are being generated is significantly higher than the processor's throughput, resulting in a continuously increasing backlog. While no alert has been raised yet and both glide.ais.event_queue_writable and glide.ais.update_event_queue_writable system properties remain true, the queue is approaching the 1 million events threshold at which the platform may automatically disable index update writability if processing stalls.

Business Impact:
New record inserts and record updates may not be reflected in AI Search results in a timely manner due to the backlog. If the queue continues to grow and processing stalls, the platform will automatically set glide.ais.update_event_queue_writable to false, at which point all Indexed Sources will become stale until the issue is resolved.

Investigation Performed:

  • Reviewed the AIS status via xmlstats.do?include=ais and confirmed both writability properties are true, AIS nodes are healthy (ACTIVE/GREEN), and the active node is processing events normally.
  • Reviewed ais_index_queue_stats over the last several hours and confirmed the queue is growing by approximately 76,000 events per hour while only ~6,000–18,000 events are being processed in that window.
  • Reviewed ais_datasource for any Indexed Source filters using JavaScript — none found, so this known cause is ruled out.
  • Reviewed ais_ingest_datasource_stats and confirmed there are no runaway or long-running indexing jobs.
  • Analyzed the contents of the ais_index queue across all sysevent shards (last 7 days) and grouped by Table and Parm1 (fields being updated) to identify the top contributors.

Root Cause:
The queue backlog is being caused by a small number of frequently-updated fields on Indexed Sources that do not require text indexing for search. By default, AI Search generates an indexing event for every INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE on an indexed table, regardless of which fields were changed. Fields updated by integrations such as LDAP/SSO, by SLA workflows, or by recursive business rules generate a high volume of unnecessary indexing events when they do not have the no_text_index attribute applied.

The top event-generating field/table combinations identified on your instance over the last 7 days are:

RankTableField(s) UpdatedEvent Count (7d)
1sys_useru_when_changed_ldap~840,000
2sc_req_itemsys_mod_count, sys_updated_by, sys_updated_on, u_step_controller~490,000
3sys_useru_when_changed_ldap, department~299,000
4sc_tasksys_mod_count, u_sla_calculation, sys_updated_by, sys_updated_on~266,000
5sc_req_itemsys_mod_count, sys_updated_by, sys_updated_on, u_service_offering_stage~239,000
6sc_req_itemsys_mod_count, variables, sys_updated_by, sys_updated_on~144,000
7sc_tasksys_mod_count, sys_updated_by, sys_updated_on, u_sla_expiration~88,000
8sc_tasksys_mod_count, sys_updated_by, sys_updated_on, u_requested_for~88,000
9sc_tasksys_mod_count, sys_updated_by, sys_updated_on, u_closed_date~85,000

The u_when_changed_ldap field on sys_user is the dominant contributor and is consistent with field updates driven by an LDAP synchronization integration. The sc_req_item and sc_task patterns are consistent with SLA / workflow business rules updating timer and state fields on each task transition.

Solution:

To resolve this issue, the no_text_index attribute needs to be added as a Field Setting on the corresponding Indexed Source (ais_datasource) for the fields that do not need to be searchable. Once applied, AI Search will immediately stop generating update events for these fields, providing immediate relief to the queue. The fields will remain searchable until you choose to reindex; reindexing is optional and only required if you want to remove the field from the search index entirely.

We have grouped the fields into two tiers based on whether they are likely to be intentionally searched on by your end users:

Tier 1 — Recommended for immediate no_text_index (no impact on user search experience):

Indexed SourceField
sys_useru_when_changed_ldap
sc_req_itemu_step_controller
sc_req_itemu_service_offering_stage
sc_req_itemu_sla_expiration
sc_req_itemu_sla_state
sc_req_itemsys_mod_count
sc_req_itemsys_updated_by
sc_tasku_sla_calculation
sc_tasku_sla_expiration
sc_tasku_closed_date
sc_tasku_service_offering_step
sc_tasksys_mod_count
sc_tasksys_updated_by

Tier 2 — Please confirm before applying (these fields may be intentionally searched on):

Indexed SourceFieldQuestion
sys_userdepartmentDo your users search the user directory by department text?
sys_useru_company_nameDo your users search the user directory by company name?
sc_req_itemvariablesDo your users search RITMs by the content of variables filled in?
sc_tasku_requested_forIs this displayed/searched as text in your search experience?

If you confirm these fields are not searched on, we recommend applying no_text_index to them as well for further queue relief.

⚠ Important — Do NOT apply no_text_index to sys_updated_on. This field must remain indexed on tables in the task hierarchy (which includes sc_req_item and sc_task) because the Retention Policy on the Indexed Source depends on it. Your current configuration already has the correct sort_by_date mapping on sys_updated_on, which should be preserved.

Recommended Follow-Up:
Once the fields above are applied, we additionally recommend reviewing KB1644352 — Identify and disable indexing on fields which are being superfluously processed by AI Search as a longer-term preventive measure. KB1644352 provides a background script that automatically identifies and applies no_text_index to commonly superfluous field types (currency, choice, integer, timer, glide_date_time, due_date, glide_duration, sys_class_name, decimal) across all your Indexed Sources. We strongly recommend running this script in a sub-production instance first in dry-run mode (default) and reviewing the proposed list of fields before applying to production.

Reference Links:

  • KB2316618 — Optimizing AI Search incremental indexing performance and addressing AIS Index Event Queue backlog issues
  • KB1644352 — Identify and disable indexing on fields which are being superfluously processed by AI Search

Next Steps:

  1. Please review the Tier 1 field list above and apply the no_text_index attribute on each field via the corresponding Indexed Source in your sub-production instance first to validate behavior.
  2. Please confirm whether the Tier 2 fields are searched on by your end users so we can finalize the recommendation for those fields.
  3. Once validated in sub-production, apply the same changes to production. The ais_index queue will begin draining once new event generation drops below the processor's throughput.
  4. Monitor queue size via the URL https://<your_instance>.service-now.com/ais_index_queue_stats_list.do and confirm the size trends downward over the following hours/days.
  5. Once the queue is at a normal level, optionally review KB1644352 and consider running the bulk script in sub-production to address any other superfluous fields across all Indexed Sources.

As part of the troubleshooting process, I and other ServiceNow personnel may need to access your instance(s) in order to review the service impact to your instance and determine the root cause. It may also be necessary to make some changes on a sub-production instance in order to troubleshoot the issue or to test a probable solution. These changes, if any, will be reverted back to the original state. If any change is not reverted a reason will be provided for the same.

Best regards,

Justin Berger
Technical Support Engineer
Working hours: 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM EST

[/code]

main.Resolution notes:
Hello Jordy, team,

please find below an explanation of the behavior:

Whenever someone triggers the ais_index.ini,  this will index all the documents listed under datasource table. 
Since it's production instance, I would suggest to wait over the weekend. It's mandatory to run init successfully (index all tables) then the AIS should be in ready state.

The reason why it's taking so long, is because cmn_location has 5m records and customer_account has 3m records, it's common to run for days to have ingestion completed for the first time running.

We cannot predict how long this will take, in large deployments the indexing can take several days, and it's advisable to keep it running. 

We are sending this in Solution Proposed, if any error happens please reject the solution and let us know so we can follow up. 

AFFECTED INSTANCES: SNC Instance - acerta.

ISSUE: After following the setup steps for Now Assist, including publishing the search profile and turning on the assistant, the AI search feature was not visible or active in the Employee Center (ESC) portal on the production instance. The feature was confirmed to be working correctly in the DEV/ACC instances with the same configuration. The status in production showed as "Enabled" but not "Ready," blocking the go-live.

SOLUTION PROPOSED: ServiceNow engineers investigated and identified that the AI Search (AIS) feature was not in a "Ready" state because the initial indexing process had not completed. The investigation revealed that someone had triggered an `ais_index.init` job, which requires indexing all documents from all data source tables. This initial ingestion is a mandatory prerequisite for AIS to become fully operational. The process was running slowly due to the large volume of records in the production instance, specifically noting that the `cmn_location` table has 5 million records and the `customer_account` table has 3 million records. It is common for this initial indexing to take several days to complete for large data sets. The `sysevent` table showed that the indexing queue was processing correctly, but slowly. The `AIS Index` job in the `sys_trigger` table was confirmed to be in a "Running" state.

NEXT STEPS: The initial indexing process is currently running and must complete successfully for AI Search to become active. We recommend allowing the process to run to completion, which may take until after the weekend. Once the indexing is finished, the AI Search status will automatically change to "Ready" and the feature will become available in the ESC portal.

Please let me know if you have any questions by updating this case.

Best regards,
Simone Caneparo

Navigate to All > AI Search > Search Experience > Search Applications. 2. Open the search application configuration you want to update. 3. In the Sort Options related list, select New. 4. Fill in the fields on the Sort Option form, specifying the field (e.g. case number) and sort order (ascending or descending). 5. Select Submit. Once configured, the sort option will appear in the sort menu for users of that application. Users can then select it to order results by case number instead of the default relevancy order. Note: If no sort options are active for a search application, the sort menu will not display and results will automatically sort by relevance. If this resolves your issue, please consider closing the Case by clicking on "Accept Solution".

**REASON FOR SOLUTION PROPOSED:**
The root cause has been identified and a configuration change will resolve this issue.

**ISSUE:**
The KB article **KB0031644** – "Como Solicitar Acesso Administrador ou Remoto" cannot be found when searching via AI Search in the Service Portal, either by article number or short description. However, the article is accessible directly via the URL:

```
https://my.whirlpool.com/sp?id=wp_kb_article_view&sysparm_article=KB0031644
```

The issue was reproduced and confirmed in the **whirlpoolqa** instance.

**ROOT CAUSE:**
During investigation, we found that **KB0031644** appears correctly in AI Search results when the user's language preference is set to **Portuguese**, but is missing when searching in other languages.

This occurs because the AI Search index source is not configured to include translated content. In order for translated articles to be returned in AI Search results across different languages, the `index_translated_reference_fields` attribute must be set on the index source.

**SOLUTION:**
To resolve this issue, please configure the AI Search index source to include translated reference fields by following the steps detailed in the official ServiceNow KB article below:

**KB2991726** – Configure AI Search to index translated reference fields

```
https://support.servicenow.com/kb?id=kb_article_view&sysparm_article=KB2991726
```

This will ensure that translated KB articles (including KB0031644) are properly indexed and returned in AI Search results, regardless of the user's language preference.

**REFERENCES:**
- KB2991726 – Configure AI Search to index translated reference fields

**NEXT STEPS:**
1. Review and apply the configuration steps outlined in KB2991726 on the affected instance(s).
2. Reindex the AI Search index source after the attribute has been applied so the translated content is picked up.
3. Validate by searching for KB0031644 (by article number and by short description) in AI Search on the Service Portal to confirm the article now appears in results across different language preferences.
4. If the resolution is confirmed in the QA instance (**whirlpoolqa**), we recommend promoting the same configuration change to your production instance.

main.Subject: Record Lookup list Issue - Configurable workspace
main.Description:
Hi Team,

     We are migrating all our support agents from native platform to configurable workspace. As part of this transitions, we are seeing some issues or gaps with in workspace compared to native platform. One such scenario involves in any reference field lookup modal in a form in workspace.

1. Let's access a record which contains a reference field and open the form in the native platform. When we click on magnifying glass icon in the field, it opens a pop up referencing to the list of records in the reference table. In native platform, we get the list, in addition to that we get a possibility to perform a column search on the fields displayed and also a generic search where we can select the field and search (a small typeahead search )
2. However, when we do the same action in workspace, the popup/modal window opens up the list of records of the reference table. But has no quick actions like column search or even a generic search in the modal window. We can still perform search on each column by selecting the available filer options and also advanced filter.

The primary difference is that number of clicks agent has to perform and based on the number of the cases they are working, it will take additional time to work on an issue or task.

We want to understand if there is a OOB configuration or work around where we can include these quick search like the new list component changes provided in Yokohoma release. In list page we have got new column search but in reference modal window or related lists it is still missing.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Access a record in platform view and click on a reference field magnifying glass and notice the search options.
https://epicorcs.service-now.com/nav_to.do?uri=x_7873_implement_n_stories.do?sys_id=47d36fb397a803107989d414a253afea
2. Access a record in workspace and click on a reference field magnifying glass and notice the quick search options. Agents has to be perform one more click to get into the filter.
https://epicorcs.service-now.com/now/cwf/agent/record/x_7873_implement_n_stories/8714233797a803107989d414a253affe
main.Resolution notes:
Hello Jagadeesh,

Thank you for your patience while I investigated this.

After reviewing the behavior on both the native platform and Configurable Workspace, I can confirm that this is expected out-of-the-box (OOB) functionality.

The reference field lookup modal in Configurable Workspace does not include the inline column search or the generic typeahead search that is available in the native platform view. In Workspace, agents are required to use the available filter options or the advanced filter to search within the reference modal. This is a known difference in the Workspace experience compared to the native platform.


As this is OOB behavior and not a defect, there is no configuration or workaround available to replicate the native platform's quick search within the reference modal in Workspace.

If you would like this functionality to be considered for a future release, I would recommend submitting an Idea on the ServiceNow Community portal at https://www.servicenow.com/community/, where product teams review customer feedback for roadmap consideration.

Please let me know if you have any further questions.

Best regards,
Lalitha
Technical Support Engineer

Two separate factors contributed to the observed behavior:

1. **Portal vs. Preview discrepancy:** The TSC portal's conversational assistant uses the **"Now Assist in VA"** AI Search Profile — not the AI Search Profile (sys_id: `fd6491cb53171010069addeeff7b123f`) and Search Source (sys_id: `47a848d653271010069addeeff7b12eb`) that were being inspected via the Search Source Preview. This is why KB0013243 surfaced in the portal but was correctly excluded from the AI Search Preview. The portal and the Preview were evaluating against different profiles, so the results were expected to differ.

2. **User Criteria evaluation:** A User Criteria diagnostic was run against the test user and KB0013243. The diagnostic confirmed that, **based on the current user criteria configuration on the article and the user's attributes, the test user is granted access**. AI Search is honoring the user criteria as configured — the configuration itself is granting the access, not bypassing it.

In short, AI Search is working as designed. The article is returned because the current user criteria configuration permits the user to read it.

**SOLUTION:**
To restrict access so that only members of "CRS Credentialing" (or any other intended audience) can read these articles, please configure the access properly
**REFERENCES:**
- ServiceNow Documentation – **Diagnose access criteria at an article level**: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/knowledge-management/diagnose-access-criteria-at-an-article-level.html

**NEXT STEPS:**

1. Use the **Diagnose access criteria** tool linked above to validate the current access behavior on KB0013243 (and any other affected articles) against the impacted user(s).
2. Adjust the **Can Read / Cannot Read** user criteria on the articles or parent Knowledge Base to enforce the intended access restrictions (e.g., by Location, Group, or Department).
3. Re-validate with an impersonated test user from the TSC portal to confirm the article is no longer returned.
4. As this issue is rooted in knowledge base access configuration rather than AI Search behavior, please **open a new case** if you would like dedicated assistance with reconfiguring the user criteria for your environment, and we will be happy to engage on that specifically.

Please let me know if you have any questions by updating this case. If this fixes the issue, please click the "Accept Solution" button. If not, please let me know so I could investigate this issue further.

The environment contains a large number of knowledge-related articles stored in custom tables created from article templates, instead of the standard Knowledge Base table (kb_knowledge). Custom tables added to the Knowledge Table Indexed Source (u_kb_template_espa_o_laser_artigo)
Custom tables added to AI Search Search Sources

Custom tables included in the Search Profile
AI Search configurations completed and published
Reindexing executed successfully
Correct language configuration applied
Search applications and facets configured correctly
The issue is inconsistent/intermittent because the functionality works correctly after reindexing sometimes, but later stops working again without additional configuration changes.

At the moment, the issue specifically affects AI Search retrieval for content stored in PDF attachments from custom knowledge-related tables.

main.Subject: Is there a supported way to increase the AI Search Retention Policy beyond the timeframe of the OOTB retention policies?
main.Description:
We have a custom table that extends task, so our AI Search indexed source is required to have a retention policy.
The maximum OOTB policy length is 3 years, but we have quite a few records that are still open but have not been updated in the last 3 years.
Is there a recommended way for us to make these records searchable in the indexed source (without updating the records)?
main.Resolution notes:
Hi @[John McDonald],

Unfortunately, this is not possible with the out-of-the-box (OOB) functionality. For the Task table and its child tables, the retention policy is mandatory, with a maximum retention period of 3 years.

This restriction has been intentionally designed because Task tables generally contain a very high volume of records. Extending retention or indexing such large datasets could potentially impact overall system performance and stability.

I hope this helps clarify the limitation. Please let me know if you would like to explore any possible alternative approaches.

Regards,
Ananda Raj G

Using AI Search to index the em_alert.work_notes field can generate a high volume of AI Search events. This significantly increases the load on AI Search nodes, which may impact both indexing and query performance on those nodes. While em_alert is a significant contributor, it is not the only source in this scenario. Updates across additional tables have also contributed to the increased load on the AI Search instances, causing disruptions in AI Search query and index processing with the AI Search node 105.1.0.2 version.

2) For the issue reported on 2026-05-25:

Our internal SME team identified an issue during the ingestion (indexing) of attachments. Specifically, the system attempted to index an attachment larger than 100MB, but the process did not complete successfully. This resulted in a disruption to the indexing workflow and led to a high queue condition.

Solution Proposed:

For the issue reported on 2026-05-14:

To address the AI Search indexing and query performance issues, our SME team implemented code optimizations on the AI Search nodes. This effort required careful development, deployment, and iterative testing to ensure the solution met both functional and quality standards.

In parallel, over the past few days, our SME team actively managed the AI Search event queue by strategically adjusting the glide.ais.event_queue_writable system property. This approach helped regulate indexing activity, maintain a balanced processing load on the nodes, control the size of the unprocessed queue, and prevent it from exceeding critical thresholds (such as 1 million events). These actions were closely monitored and guided by our internal SME team.

To resolve the issue, our SME team deployed the AI Search node version 105.1.0.4, which has been specifically optimized to better handle the observed load conditions identified as the most likely cause.

main.Subject: ricted Knowledge Content Surfaced in GenAI Results
main.Description: Now Assist Security Issue: Restricted Knowledge Content Surfaced in GenAI Results. Now Assist is surfacing restricted knowledge articles as sources for users who do not meet the defined User Criteria.
main.Resolution notes:
Hello Shawn,

Following our investigation, including re-indexing the specific Knowledge Base article in question, we were able to confirm that the observed behavior is expected. The system is designed to surface content in GenAI responses based on what the user already has access to through AI Search, and since the article is accessible, it is expected to appear in the results.

At this time, there is no supported method to explicitly restrict or hide Knowledge content within the chat experience beyond what is already controlled through AI Search and standard access permissions. To prevent certain Knowledge content from appearing, the recommended approach is to exclude the Knowledge table from the configured search source so it is no longer indexed or surfaced in AI Search results. This behavior is also documented in the following community reference: 

https://www.servicenow.com/community/employee-center-forum/how-to-hide-kb-article-in-ai-search/m-p/3488093,

This community article confirms that there is no direct way to hide individual KB articles from AI Search and recommends managing visibility through search source configuration instead.

To update the search source configuration, you can navigate to AI Search > Search Sources, locate the relevant search source used by your experience, open the record, and review the Tables or Source Configuration related list. From there, remove or exclude the Knowledge [kb_knowledge] table from the source, then save the changes and trigger a re-index to ensure the updates take effect.

Based on the above will move this to a solution proposed state.

Thanks,
Jaime

This is a common observation in AI Search event logs. Here are few  causes mentioned

parm1 empty + parm2 = update → profile-level index refresh, no source table context
parm1 = example:- sc_cat_item_producer + parm2 = delete → record-level event, table is derivable but still may not populate the Table column depending on how the event was fired

Synonym dictionary updates
Search profile configuration changes
Stopword or boost weight changes

main.Subject: Scheduling Jobs for Indexing of AI Search Indexed Sources
main.Description: We are looking to understand how OOB Indexing happens automatically for AI Search Indexed Source. Also if there is any scheduled job available which we can customize accordingly.
main.Resolution notes:
Hello Arijit,

We are placing this case in a Solution Proposed state as we have provided guidance regarding AI Search indexing.

AFFECTED INSTANCES: SNC Instance - jwithelp, SNC Instance - jwithelpdev.

ISSUE: A request for information on how out-of-the-box (OOB) indexing happens automatically for AI Search Indexed Sources and whether a scheduled job is available for customization.

SOLUTION PROPOSED: Investigation confirmed that AI Search indexing is an automated process triggered by record changes and managed by internal scheduled jobs. For each Indexed Source, AI Search incrementally indexes records (Inserts, Updates, Deletes) by generating events in the `ais_index` queue. These events are processed by the "AIS Index Event Processor" job, which runs approximately every 30 seconds. This ensures that record changes are quickly reflected in search results.

Additionally, two daily scheduled jobs, "AIS Index Purge Stale Document" and "AIS Create Index Updatable Field Event," manage data retention policies and update dynamic fields. While manual re-indexing for single or multiple sources is possible via the UI, the underlying code and APIs that control this process are protected and not accessible for customer customization in a scheduled job. This is a platform design to ensure system stability. Please see KB2316618 for reference.

- https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/ai-search/indexing-content-ais.html
- https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/ai-search/index-single-source-ais.html
- https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/ai-search/index-multiple-sources-ais.html

NEXT STEPS: Please review the provided explanation and the referenced documentation links regarding the automated nature of AI Search indexing.

Please let me know if you have any questions by updating this case.

Best regards,
Galimbek Sagidenov

main.Resolution notes:
Hello Sweta,

We are placing this case in a Solution Proposed state as we have provided guidance regarding the product's designed behavior.

AFFECTED INSTANCES: SNC Instance - aegondev, SNC Instance - aegonmodel.

ISSUE: A request for guidance on enabling AI Search for CMDB tables. Contradictory information was found between official ServiceNow documentation, which states CMDB tables are excluded, and a community post suggesting a system property 'glide.ais.ingestion.should_index' could enable it.

SOLUTION PROPOSED: Investigation confirmed that, by design, AI Search does not support indexing the base CMDB table or its descendants.

AFFECTED INSTANCES: SNC Instance - alliantuat.

ISSUE: The AIS Index Event queue on the alliantuat instance was not writable. This was triggered by an automatic process that disabled the queue when the number of unprocessed events exceeded one million, preventing new search indexing events from being processed.

SOLUTION PROPOSED: we investigated and identified that the AIS Index Event queue on the alliantuat instance was not writable. The system property `glide.ais.update_event_queue_writable` was automatically set to `false` because the event queue size surpassed one million events. Investigation revealed that a high volume of events was being generated by updates to the `sys_user_group` table, specifically from the fields `sys_mod_count`, `u_last_ldap_sync`, `sys_updated_by`, and `sys_updated_on`.

To prevent future occurrences, you added the `no_text_index` attribute to the problematic fields on the `sys_user_group` and `sys_user` tables, and cleared the backlog of events. A change request (CHG74058374) was then attempted to re-enable the queue by setting `glide.ais.update_event_queue_writable` back to `true`. This first attempt was unsuccessful due to a custom business rule on your instance that prevented the property from being modified.

After you granted the necessary access and disabled the preventative business rule, a second change request (CHG74331945) was executed. This change successfully set the `glide.ais.update_event_queue_writable` property back to `true`. Post-change monitoring confirmed that the queued records are now processing as expected.

NEXT STEPS: The AIS event queue is now processing correctly. If the provided solution is satisfactory, you can accept it to bring this case to closure.

main.Description:
When using the Search we are getting some unexpected outcomes. Please see attached document with some test scenarios.
Also we have notice when testing catalog item search (name, meta) is not returning valid outputs.
main.Resolution notes:
Hello,

We are placing this into Solution Proposed as we believe the information provided below will resolve your issue. If you have any questions or need anything else related to this Case, kindly contact us or update the case and we will be happy to assist you further. If this resolves your issue, please consider closing the Case by clicking on "Accept Solution".

**REASON FOR SOLUTION PROPOSED:**
The root cause has been identified and you have confirmed that applying the proposed solution resolved the issue.

**ISSUE:**
Search on the Employee Center portal (/esc) was not returning expected results for Knowledge Base Articles (KBAs) and catalog items. Catalog item searches by item name and meta fields returned no valid results (e.g., searching "service offering" returned nothing), and certain KBAs did not appear in full search results even when an exact match was shown.

**ROOT CAUSE:**
The issue stemmed from two separate configuration conditions affecting search indexing:

1. **Catalog items / KBA "service offering" search** — The category associated with the affected items was disabled, which prevented the items from being indexed and returned in search.

2. **KBA search (e.g., KB1001445)** — The article was in a "Review" workflow state rather than "Published." The Next Experience Search Profile used by Global Search only indexes articles in a "Published" state, so the article was excluded from full search results.

3. **KBA search (e.g., KB1001321)** — Although this article was correctly in a "Published" state, its parent Knowledge Base category was inactive. An inactive parent category prevents the article from being included in the search index.

**SOLUTION:**
To resolve the issue, the following actions were applied:

1. Enable the disabled category associated with the affected catalog items.
2. Ensure the affected KBAs are in a "Published" workflow state.
3. Activate the inactive parent Knowledge Base category.
4. Re-index the Knowledge Base data source so the corrected records are picked up.
5. Verify all search source criteria before re-testing.

**NEXT STEPS:**
You have confirmed that the above actions resolved both the catalog item and KBA search behavior, so we will proceed with closing this case. If you encounter similar search indexing behavior with other items in the future, please verify the relevant category state, the article workflow state, and re-index the data source as a first step.

main.Subject: KB article is not indexed and doesn't show in global search or agent assist
main.Description:
KB0012756 does not show up in CSM workspace Global Search or Agent assent when using the search phrases or "app crashes on download".  

When searching for the KB number it does work. 

Why are the key words and search phrases not working to locate the KB? This has happened numerous times. We need to find root cause as I suspect it's something to do with indexing that's being missed.
main.Resolution notes:
Hi Stephen,

Thank you for your continued patience while we investigated this case.

I reviewed the AI Search indexing health on the instance. Unfortunately, I was unable to retrieve historical indexing details from the time the previous knowledge article was published. However, I would like to share a few guidelines that may help validate the behavior if it is observed again in the future:

1) AI Search does not automatically index historical records that existed before an indexed source was configured or before a full table index was performed.
2)Tables that have never undergone a full table index may have records that are not searchable until a full indexing operation is completed.
3) New, updated, or deleted knowledge articles are typically processed through incremental indexing, which runs approximately every 30 seconds.
4) Changes to index configurations—such as adding indexed fields, modifying indexed attributes, or updating source settings—often require a full reindex before the changes are reflected in search results.
5) Delays in indexing can occasionally occur due to high volumes of records in the event queue (sysevent). In these situations, knowledge article indexing requests may be queued and processed as resources become available. This is most commonly seen during large integration activities or bulk updates affecting heavily used tables, such as sys_user

If you encounter this behavior again, please open a new case so we can proactively review the health and performance of the AI Search indexing process while the issue is occurring. You can note of the count in sysevent and filter just ais_index to know if there is a lag. 

Thank you,

main.Subject: AI Search Issue
main.Description: Getting URL blocked when clicked on any link displayed in AI Search
main.Resolution notes:
Hello Subhash,

I hope you are doing well.

Thank you for your patience while I continued reviewing this behavior internally.

After detailed investigation and validation, I would like to share the findings regarding the issue where URLs from AI Search / Genius results are not opening in a new tab and the related workaround implementation.

Root Cause:

The behavior itself is related to the current product design of Now Assist / AI Search Genius results, where links open in the same browser tab by default unless additional customization is introduced.

As referenced in KB2683514, a workaround is available which involves customizing the OOB **Faceted Search** Service Portal widget by modifying the Client Controller logic to force result links to open in a new tab.

However, while attempting to apply this workaround in testing, the implementation could not be completed successfully because the instance encounters a known platform issue while updating the OOB widget.

During Save/Update of the widget, the following compile error is triggered:

> Could not save record because of a compile error: JavaScript parse error at line (721) column (55) problem = syntax error (<refname>: line 721)

This issue is already identified internally and aligns with the following known PRB:

* PRB1926836 – Update on SP widget "Faceted Search" not possible and widget gets skipped on upgrade

Due to this platform-level widget compilation issue, the workaround customization mentioned in the KB currently cannot be implemented successfully in the impacted environment.

 Validation Performed:

* Reproduced the reported behavior internally
* Reviewed and validated KB2683514
* Tested the workaround implementation on the Faceted Search widget
* Confirmed the JavaScript compile/parsing error during widget update
* Verified internally that Development is already aware of the issue and actively working on the PRB

Related KB / PRB References:

* KB2683514 – Using Now Assist in AI Search – Genius result links should open in a new tab
* PRB1926836 – Update on SP widget "Faceted Search" not possible and widget gets skipped on upgrade

This is the prb which is mentioned below
https://support.servicenow.com/problem.do?sysparm_query=number=PRB1961276

Solution Proposed:

At this stage, the recommended approach would be to wait for the permanent fix from the Development team for the identified PRB.

Once the PRB fix is delivered in an upcoming release/patch, the workaround described in KB2683514 can then be implemented successfully without encountering the widget compile error.

After the fix becomes available:

* The Faceted Search widget customization can be applied safely
* AI Search / Genius result links can then be configured to open in a new browser tab as expected

I have also attached the related screenshots and validation details for reference.

Please let me know if you have any further questions or observations from your end.

We are looking to enable AI Search for Next Experience in PROD. We have been testing in DEV and QA, and noticed the following:

2) When searching a RITM # as an ITIL fulfillers, search results DO NOT show related SCTASKs.

The latter situation only works if you are an admin. I'm not sure why regular ITIL users (such as user: Joanne Evans) cannot see a related SCTASK when she types in a RITM # into the unified navigational search bar, but when she types in the associated REQ # to that RITM, it will show her SCTASKs?

NOTE: I am out of office for the next week - please keep this ticket open in the meantime, until I come back on June 3. This is a business critical issue because we will be having a go-live of AI Search for Next Experience on June 5. This issue is currently a blocker to our go-live.
main.Resolution notes:
[code]

Hello Melissa,

Thank you very much for your patience while I continued investigating this behavior. I truly appreciate your time and collaboration throughout this process.

During the debugging of AI Search using the Search Preview, I identified the following entries in the logs:

  • AIS: ACL – possible late-binding for table/field: sc_task.request_item due to script on ACL term 94665fdddbf48a58abe26c391396190c
  • AIS: ACL – possible late-binding for table/field: sc_task.request_item due to script on ACL term d9694407c3923000c111113e5bba8ffd

These log entries point to the following ACLs, which are configured as scripted ACLs:

  • View ACL records

As per platform design, AI Search does not support scripted field-level ACLs or conditional field-level ACLs. This limitation is documented here for your reference:

  • AI Search content security documentation

Based on these findings, the behavior observed is expected. Since certain fields are governed by unsupported ACL types, AI Search is unable to fully evaluate access to those fields. As a result, the system may determine that the related item should not be included in the results, as it cannot confirm full access for the user.

Please feel free to let me know if you you have any additional questions about it. I would be more than happy to assist.

Thank you again for your continued partnership.

Best regards,

Senior Technical Support Engineer – Platform Tech
