main.Resolution notes: Ueda 様 平素よりお世話になっております。テクニカルサポート鈴木です。お問合せに回答いたします。 [code]回答: [/code] ご質問①：Zurich以降のバージョンであれば AI Platform は問題なく利用可能か ＜回答＞ ご認識のとおり、Zurich 以降のバージョンであれば AI Platform（Now Assist、AI Search 等の AI 機能群）はご利用いただけます。バージョン要件としての問題はございません。 なお、補足として以下の前提条件がございます。 - 生成AI系の機能（Now Assist）のご利用には、該当する サブスクリプション／SKU 契約（例：Now Assist for Platform 等）が必要です。プラットフォーム標準のままでは生成AI機能は有効化されません。 - Now Assist の画面体験（Now Assist Panel やフォーム内のAI機能等）は Next Experience UI が前提となります。お客様がご利用中の古いUI（UI16）の環境では、これらの生成AI体験は表示されません。「古いUIでは今後の最新AI機能が使用で きなくなる」というお話につきましては、この点においてご認識のとおりでございます。AI機能をフルにご活用いただくには、Next Experience UI への移行をご検討いただく形となります。 ご質問②：カスタムテーブルのデータを用いる場合の制限事項 ＜回答＞ カスタムテーブル上のデータでも AI 機能はご利用いただけますが、機能ごとに対応方法が異なりますので、下記にご案内いたします。 - AI Search：カスタムテーブルを「Indexed Source（インデックス対象ソース）」として登録いただくことで、カスタムテーブルのレコードを検索対象にできます。どのフィールドをインデックスするかは Semantic Index 設定で構成いただきます。 - Now Assist の標準スキル：要約・回答生成などの標準スキルは、特定の標準テーブル（incident、case、kb_knowledge 等）に紐付いて提供されております。そのままではカスタムテーブルには適用されません。 - カスタムテーブルで生成AIをご利用の場合：上記の標準スキルをそのまま流用することはできないため、Now Assist Skill Kit を用いた独自スキルの作成、および Now Assist Data Kit によるデータ構成が必要となります。 ご質問③：設定手順のドキュメント ＜回答＞ 各機能のセットアップ手順は、下記の公式ドキュメントにてご確認いただけます。 - Now Assist（製品・スキル一覧、有効化手順） https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/zurich/intelligent-experiences/platform-now-assist-landing.html - AI Search 概要 https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/zurich/platform-administration/ai-search/overview-ais.html - Managing indexed sources（カスタムテーブルを検索対象に登録する手順） https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/ai-search/ais-managing-indexed-source.html 上記回答を持ちまして、本件のステータスをSolution Proposedとさせていただきます。 本件について、ご不明な点等ございましたらお気軽にお問合せください。 問題ないようでしたら、Accept Solutionボタンを押下し本件をクローズして頂けますと幸いです。 以上、よろしくお願いいたします。 鈴木卓人 | Technical Support, APJ Delivery Services 日本語サポート時間：祝日を除く平日午前9時より午後5時まで

main.Subject: Attempting to run AI search on a search term while filtering results on input
main.Description:
I'm attempting to use AI search to match user issues semantically against the Incident table. I'm looking for incidents over the past 24 hours for a specific user who is the caller or affected user. That user will change dynamically depending on who's using a specific catalog item. I have the user input already and the search term, I just need to know how to plug this into AI Search. I tried using the action listed below in Flow Designer since this seems to be the best way to do this. However, there's no documentation that I can find for how to use this spoke, and I can't get it to work. The major sticking point with most other methods like an AI retriever skill or PI Similarity solutions seems to be that I can't dynamically change the user. How do I either accomplish this a different way or use the below action properly.

https://northwelldev2.service-now.com/now/workflow-studio/builder%3Ftable%3Dsys_hub_flow%26sysId%3D06802a5ec3c1c3501ac2e72bb0013158
main.Resolution notes:
Thanks for the follow up Evan. 

We connected with our Dev specialists to help answer your latest questions. 

We will include a summary of your case details and the original questions you asked along with the answers to your latest query. 

ISSUE:

Need to understand the following about the AI Search action available within Workflow studio:

1. Was it intended to be available for use?
2. Is there anything else they could use instead? Or other ways to hook into AIS other than the flow
3. If they shouldn't be doing this the customer would like to know why

SOLUTION PROPOSED:

The "AI Search" action visible in Workflow Studio is the atlas_search hub action (sys_hub_action_type_definition:c93fa3795b221010a76b04d13d81c767).

Context: This action was built for the VA Server to call AI Search asynchronously when no intent is found during a Virtual Agent conversation.

The required fields the you are further explained:

- search term — the user's input string to search
- context_profile_id — a search context configuration ID. In VA flows, this is resolved automatically by looking up mapped
IDs from the Custom Chat Experience settings (or falling back to defaults). Outside of VA, there would need to be a
manually provide a valid search context config ID, but this is not documented.
- start time — timestamp for the search request

This action is set to access=public and state=published, which is why it appears in the Workflow Studio action picker.

However, it was designed for internal use by VA topic flows and is tightly coupled to the VA runtime (e.g., it expects VA-specific context for resolving search profiles).

There is no supported way to configure this action for use outside of Virtual Agent, and no documentation exists because it was not designed for that use case.

Addressing your questions directly below:

1. Was it intended to be available for use? 
- Yes, but only within Virtual Agent topic flows. Its visibility in Workflow Studio is a side effect of the access=public setting needed for the VA topic block system to invoke it.

2. Is there anything else you could use instead? 
- There are no officially supported, documented REST APIs for invoking AI Search programmatically outside of Virtual Agent at this time.
- The following community article includes an undocumented internal endpoint which technically will work however this is unsupported, ServiceNow can change or remove it without notice, and there is no official documentation or support commitment for it.
-https://www.servicenow.com/community/developer-forum/are-there-any-rest-apis-for-ai-search/m-p/2090165

3. If you shouldn't be using this, why is it exposed? 
- The action needs to be public for VA's internal topic block orchestration. There is no mechanism to make it visible to VA
while hiding it from Workflow Studio.

Ultimately the supported path for AI Search outside of VA today is through native search UI surfaces (e.g., the AI Search application, portal search bars), not via a REST API.

Next Steps:

If there is a need for programmatic AI Search access outside of VA, the best path is to submit a product enhancement request through the ServiceNow Idea Portal: 

https://support.servicenow.com/ideas

Please let us know if any further assistance is needed and we will help as best we can. 

Otherwise if no further assistance is required feel free to accept the solution to close out your case. 

Best,
Brendan

main.Subject: Searching terms on Knowledge Center gets substituted
main.Description: When searching for articles on the Knowledge Center, the word 'journey' always gets substituted by the word 'corner'. This behaviour only seems to affect that term. It is quite strange and would like to know the root cause to prevent it in the future.
main.Resolution notes: Hello Javier, We are moving your case to Solution Proposed as we believe the information provided below will resolve your issue. If we have addressed your concerns, you may accept the solution to close this case or reject the solution if it does not answer the original question raised with this ticket. At any time in the Solution Proposed state, you may add additional questions or updates. [code]Issue: [/code] In the Knowledge Center search bar, searching for "student journey" automatically returns results for "student corner" instead. The UI displays "Showing results for student corner" with a "Search instead for student journey" [code]Steps to Reproduce:[/code] 1.Navigate to Knowledge Center 2.Search for "student journey" 3.System queries "student corner" and returns results for that term instead [code]Solution Proposed: [/code] Thank you for reporting this issue. After investigating the AI Search configuration on your instance, I believe I have identified the root cause. The Knowledge Portal Search Profile uses a Derived Spell Check dictionary, which is automatically built from the content indexed in the kb_knowledge table. Since the term "journey" did not appear frequently enough in your knowledge base for the spell check engine to recognise it as a valid term, it was being treated as a potential typo and substituted with the closest matching term it knew — in this case, "corner", likely because "student corner" appears in your knowledge base content. As a resolution, I added "journey" and "journeys" as Blocked Terms in the Typo Handling dictionary on your dev instance at the following link: https://sommetdev.service-now.com/ais_dictionary_term_list.do?sysparm_query=dictionary.nameSTARTSWITHsn_km_portal_knowledge_portal_search_profile_default_spell_check_dictionary&sysparm_first_row=1&sysparm_view=&sysparm_choice_query_raw=&sysparm_list_header_search=true https://sommetdev.service-now.com/ais_dictionary.do?sys_id=9726393477e40210694782c79f5a9948&sysparm_record_list=type%3dSpellcheck%5esys_idIN9865058bc7031010d1cfd9795cc26037%2c9726393477e40210694782c79f5a9948%2cb29df374c7531010d1cfd9795cc260cd%2c%5eORDERBYname&sysparm_record_row=1&sysparm_record_rows=1&sysparm_record_target=ais_dictionary&sysparm_view=Spellcheck&sysparm_view_forced=true https://sommetdev.service-now.com/ais_search_profile.do?sys_id=d2a4fdb077e40210694782c79f5a99b3&sysparm_record_target=ais_search_profile&sysparm_record_row=12&sysparm_record_rows=13&sysparm_record_list=ORDERBYname This prevents the spell check engine from rewriting those terms during a search query. Below you can find useful documents: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/zurich/platform-administration/ai-search/typo-handling-ais.html?contentId=lhRp8FYOaPQbRS~q_A9FFg https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/yokohama/platform-administration/ai-search/exclude-typo-handling-terms-ais.html?contentId=fCoy5AEhIha0_uZToVjBsA [code]Next Steps: [/code] Please test this behavior on your DEV instance and confirm if it now works as expected. Once you approve, we can proceed with moving this configuration change to your other environments. main.Subject: We are unable to replicate the Org Chart user visibility in the AI Search People Search Source due to custom fields not being evaluated in Search Source filter conditions.
main.Description:
We are unable to replicate the Org Chart user visibility in the AI Search People Search Source due to custom fields not being evaluated in Search Source filter conditions. Please find the below details.

Background:
The requirement is to hide robotic/system users from the AI Search People results and show only the same users visible on the Org Chart. To achieve this, we attempted to apply the following filter on the People Search Source — which mirrors the existing Org Chart filter logic:

active=true^u_report_group!=SYSTEM^u_worker_type=fte^u_adstartdate<=javascript:gs.endOfToday()^NQactive=true^u_report_group!=SYSTEM^u_worker_type=cw^u_emp_type!=C-Functional ID^u_emp_typeSTARTSWITHC^u_actual_start_date<=javascript:gs.endOfToday()

 

Problem:
The filter is not producing the expected results. After investigation, we identified the root cause:

 

1. Custom fields (u_ prefixed fields such as u_report_group, u_worker_type, u_emp_type, u_adstartdate, u_actual_start_date) are not part of the OOB sys_user Indexed Source in AI Search. Due to which the results are not showing any of the people even if they come under that filter.

 

Ask:
We would like ServiceNow to advise on the supported approach to filter People Search Source results using custom user attributes, specifically:

 

- Can custom u_ fields be added to the sys_user Indexed Source Field Settings & Mapping to support filter conditions on the Search Source?
- If yes, what is the recommended process and are there any upgrade or support implications?

- if no, can we utilize any OOTB fields to mark robotic users and use that field as to hide the robotic users in ai search config 
- Is there a supported mechanism to replicate Org Chart visibility logic (which relies on custom fields and relative date expressions) within AI Search People results?
main.Resolution notes:
Hello Jeevan,

I am moving this case in solution propose status with comment on your queries:

Can custom u_ fields be added to the sys_user Indexed Source Field Settings & Mapping to support filter conditions on the Search Source?

main.Resolution notes:
Hi Jean-Francois,

We are placing this case in a Solution Proposed state and will include a summary of your case details for our records. 

ISSUE: 

Knowledge articles created on custom article templates not appearing in Employee Center AI search results

SOLUTION PROPOSED: 

The behavior observed is expected with the child tables being required to be present in the indexed source when indexing in order for the KB's to be searchable. 

In Yokohama (cnstg, cn), the OOTB Knowledge indexed source was more permissive about auto-including child tables, so articles in custom template tables like u_kb_template_policy, u_kb_template_job_aid, etc., were returned in AI Search without explicit configuration.

In Australia (cndev, cnuat), AI Search extracts and indexes content from records in the parent table and only those child tables you explicitly configure for indexing — the behavior is now strictly opt-in for child tables. 

This is consistent with how AI Search is documented to work, and the Australia upgrade appears to have enforced this more strictly. 

NEXT STEPS: 

Moving forward please define any child tables in the indexed sources.

Hello Pete,

We are placing this issue in Solution Proposed as we believe the information provided below will resolve your issue. If you have any questions or need anything else related to this Case kindly contact us or update the case and we will be happy to assist you further. If this resolves your issue, please consider closing the Case by clicking on Accept Solution.

AFFECTED INSTANCES: aamcdev.

ISSUE: New knowledge articles not showing in Now Assist for Virtual Agent or AI Search results.

SOLUTION PROPOSED: 
=> The root cause of the issue is that an oversized attachment on a knowledge article was blocking the AI Search ingestion queue.

=> A draft KB article (KB0010054, "Administrator Guide to ServiceNow") has a 251 MB PDF attachment (servicenow-zurich-it-service-management-enus.pdf):-
https://aamcdev.service-now.com/kb_knowledge_list.do?sysparm_query=sys_id%3Dcdf80ddf2b8547500ce2fe72f291bfe1&sysparm_first_row=1&sysparm_view=

=> Because the indexed source's filter includes KB articles in draft state as well, this draft article was included in indexing. 
=> Every 30-second processor cycle attempted to upload the 251 MB file to the AI Search node, which dropped the TCP connection mid-stream. 

=> This triggered a 10-minute retry loop that prevented all ~12,500 queued indexing events from being processed.
AI Search Indexed Retry Histories:-
https://aamcdev.service-now.com/ais_ingest_retry_stats_list.do?sysparm_query=&sysparm_first_row=1&sysparm_view=

=>I have removed the 2 stuck attachment indexing events from the sysevent queue. This unblocked the ingestion pipeline and allowed new KB articles to become searchable (attached screenshot for reference).

=> Fix the indexed source filter with the condition Workflow is Published which ensures only published articles are indexed going forward.
https://aamcdev.service-now.com/ais_datasource.do?sys_id=975c0985772300102d71af6168106191

=> Remove the oversized attachment from the KB article KB0010054 or replace the 251 MB PDF attachment servicenow-zurich-it-service-management-enus.pdf with a smaller file. 

=> As long as this large file exists on any article that matches the indexed source filter, it will re-enter the queue and block ingestion again.

main.Subject: AI Search External Content - Delta Sync Support
main.Description:
Hi,

We are ingesting Brainstorm/Learning content videos into AI Search using the "BrainStorm Ingest" flow. The planned ingest schedule is monthly.

I would like to confirm whether delta sync is supported out of the box for this setup.

Specifically, if one import returns 98 items and the next run returns 97, will the missing item be automatically removed from the AI Search index or do we need to explicitly track and delete removed items in the flow? 

If OOB delta sync is not available, please advise the recommended implementation approach.

Related cases:

CS9169293
CS9157963

Thank you,
Thrishal
main.Resolution notes:
Hello Thrishal, 

We are providing the solution below, as we believe the information provided will effectively resolve your issue.

Issue: You are ingesting Brainstorm/Learning content videos into AI Search using the "BrainStorm Ingest" flow on a monthly schedule. You are requesting confirmation on whether delta sync is supported out of the box for this setup. Specifically, you would like to know whether AI Search automatically handles the removal of items from the index when they are no longer present in a subsequent import. For example, if one import returns 98 items and the next run returns 97, you would like to know if the missing item is automatically removed from the AI Search index or whether your flow needs to explicitly track and delete removed items. If out of the box delta sync is not available, you are requesting guidance on the recommended implementation approach to handle this scenario.

Related Cases:
CS9169293
CS9157963

Steps to Reproduce: N/A

Solution Proposed/Next Steps: Thank you for your patience. Below are the responses from our Development team regarding your inquiries.

Question 1: Is delta sync supported out of the box?

Answer: No. BrainStorm content is ingested into AI Search through the External Content Ingestion API as a push operation against the external data source, BrainStorm Content (schema table u_brainstorm_articles). AI Search stores exactly the documents that are pushed to it and does not compare one import run against a previous run.

Question 2: Does AI Search automatically remove items that are no longer present in a later import?

Answer: No. AI Search will not remove an item simply because it is absent from a subsequent import run. For example, if an import initially contains 98 items and a later import contains only 97 items, the item that was removed from the source will remain in the AI Search index.

We also reviewed the BrainStorm Ingest flow on a test instance. The flow initializes a batcher, retrieves content from the source platform, ingests each item, commits the batch, and releases the batcher. There are currently no steps in the flow that remove or delete documents. As a result, stale items are not removed, and the index will continue to accumulate content that no longer exists in the source system.

Question 3: What is the recommended implementation approach?

Answer: The flow should be enhanced to explicitly remove items that are no longer present in the source. The External Content Ingestion API currently used by the flow provides several deletion operations, including:

- removeDocument (by document ID)
- deleteByQuery
- deleteByAISQuery
- purgeAllDocuments

The recommended approach is for the flow to track the set of document IDs ingested during each run and, on subsequent runs, delete any IDs that were present previously but are no longer returned by the source. Alternatively, a full rebuild approach could be implemented, where all existing documents are removed and re-ingested during each run, provided the process is properly sequenced to avoid conflicts between deletions and new ingests.

Please let me know if these responses address all of your questions or if you need any additional clarification or assistance.

main.Description: AI search results are not showing accurately on ESC portal
main.Resolution notes:
Hello Rohit,

We are placing this case in a Solution Proposed state as we have identified the cause of the issue
And our sincere apologies for the delay in response


Below is the Root Cause Summary for this event.

Root Cause:

When Hybrid Search is enabled, the results are coming from Now LLM/Semantic Search. Earlier, the Document match threshold value was set to 0, so the search was not applying a proper matching threshold and was returning a very broad set of records available on the ESC portal.

This is why, while searching for the keyword Salesforce, the result count was very high and around 868 articles were returned.

Solution Proposed:

The Document match threshold needs to be configured on the Semantic Search Configuration record. This value should be between 0 and 1.

For testing, we updated the value to 0.72. After this change, the same Salesforce search now returns around 81 results, which is the expected behavior because the search is now filtering results based on the configured document match threshold.

Please go ahead and set the appropriate Document match threshold value as per your business requirement.

https://bygeniedev.service-now.com/ais_semantic_search_configuration.do?sysparm_nostack=true&sys_id=6b2c447ab7332210e33df89f9e11a931&sysparm_record_target=ais_semantic_search_configuration&sysparm_record_row=1&sysparm_record_rows=2&sysparm_record_list=ORDERBYname

Note :- Document match threshold should be in between -1 to 1.

main.Resolution notes:
Hi,

Thank you for your patience while we investigated the Knowledge Base search issue reported in INC6092920.

**Issue Summary**
Knowledge Base articles were not appearing in Global Search results when users searched using keywords from article metadata fields, even after a reindex was completed.

**Root Cause Analysis**
During our investigation, we identified two key findings:

1. **Article Active Status**: Article KB0014802 was configured with `Active = false`, which prevents it from being indexed by AI Search. Articles must be set to `Active = true` to be searchable.

2. **Global Search Configuration**: The Next Experience Search Profile was not published, which means Global Search was not utilizing AI Search. This is a configuration issue separate from the Knowledge Base indexing process.

**Resolution**
To resolve this issue, please ensure the following:

- Verify that all Knowledge Base articles intended for search are set to `Active = true` in the Knowledge Base module.
- Publish the Next Experience Search Profile to enable Global Search to use AI Search.
- After making these configuration changes, trigger a Knowledge Base reindex to ensure all active articles are properly indexed.

Once these steps are completed, users should be able to find Knowledge Base articles by searching with keywords from article metadata fields in Global Search.

**Next Steps**
Please implement the above recommendations and test the search functionality with your users. If you continue to experience issues or have questions about configuring the Search Profile, please let us know and we'll be happy to assist further.

main.Subject: Employee Center Search
main.Description:
Hello,

Issue Summary
Inconsistent knowledge article visibility in Employee Center search when impersonating different users.

Description
When performing a search for "sap hana" in Employee Center while impersonating Cheryl Payton, the knowledge article KB0010932 appears in the search results.
However, when performing the same search while impersonating Charae Jackson, KB0010932 does not appear in the search results.

Expected Behavior
Both users should see KB0010932.

Actual Behavior
Cheryl Payton: KB0010932 is visible in search results
Charae Jackson: KB0010932 is NOT visible in search results

Additional Context
Both users are associated with DataGov role
The search term used was identical: "sap hana"

Request
Please investigate why KB0010932 is visible to one user but not the other, despite both being in the same group (DataGov).

Thanks,
David
main.Resolution notes:
Hi David,

After further investigation, we found what was causing the issue.

Root cause:

ServiceNow's user_roles field type (kb_knowledge.roles is this type) stores role names as literal strings, not as references. Therefore, when DataGov was entered during KB creation, it remained in uppercase in the database, and this literal case is preserved even if the role itself is renamed elsewhere — there is no automatic sync.

AI Search preserves this literal case when indexing the KB (the indexed value is DataGov), but when constructing user context, it forces all role names to lowercase (the value in user context is datagov). AIS facet matching is case-sensitive exact matching (default behavior of the Zing engine): FACET(datagov) does not match DataGov → the KB is filtered by the security filter → the KB does not appear in search results.

Why can CPAYTON search but CJACKSON cannot?

Both users have the DataGov role, but CPAYTON additionally possesses two OOTB roles: knowledge_admin and knowledge_manager. ServiceNow's kb_knowledge security model grants special exemptions for these two roles — when a user possesses either one, AIS completely bypasses the check on the roles field (the security query becomes MATCHALL(), allowing all KBs), so CPAYTON's query never triggers the case-comparison logic.
While CJACKSON lacks these two admin roles, so her query must pass through full facet validation, where it fails due to the case inconsistency.

When AIS indexes the roles field of a KB, it preserves the case as-is. If the KB contains DataGov, the indexed value is also DataGov.
User Side (Searcher): When AIS constructs user context, it forces all role names to lowercase. Even if sys_user_role.name is DataGov, it becomes datagov when added to the user context.

During search, AIS attempts to match the user's datagov (lowercase) against the KB index's DataGov (uppercase). This is case-sensitive exact matching in the Zing engine, they don't match → the KB is filtered out.

Solution:

Rename role name "DataGov" to lowercase "datagov" in sys_user_role table, then add lowercase "datagov" to the "role" field in KB0010932 (or alternatively, simply replace the "DataGov" in the KB's role field with "datagov" without modifying the actual role name in sys_user_role) to restore search functionality.

As a best practice, please kindly use lowercase role names

We're moving this case to Solution Proposed as we believe the information provided should help resolve your issue. Please note that Solution Proposed does not mean the case is closed. If you have further questions or concerns, there's no need to reject the solution to get assistance. Simply reply to this message, and I will be happy to assist you further.

If the proposed solution works for you, we'd appreciate it if you could close the case by clicking Accept Solution.

Regards,
Yannick

main.Description: Event Queue Performance
main.Resolution notes:
Hello Mayuri,

We are placing this case in a Solution Proposed state as the root cause has been identified and a resolution implemented.

AFFECTED INSTANCES: SNC Instance - metrolinx.

ISSUE: An alert was generated for event queue performance on the metrolinx instance, indicating a delay in processing system events which could impact email, text indexing, and flow executions. The backlog was growing, with the number of events being created outpacing the number being processed.

SOLUTION PROPOSED: ServiceNow engineers investigated and identified that the event queue backlog was caused by a large influx of `ais_index` events. At the peak of the issue, there were over 70,000 unprocessed `ais_index` events. Analysis confirmed that the event processors were active and not stuck, but the intake rate was overwhelming the processing capacity. The system was observed to be self-recovering as the processing rate eventually exceeded the creation rate, clearing the backlog. The alert was cleared once the event queue returned to a healthy state.

NEXT STEPS: The event queue has been cleared and is now operating normally. If the provided solution is satisfactory, you can accept it to bring this case to closure.

main.Resolution notes:
Hi Maria,
Thanks for your patience on this!  Below is a response to your question:

2. "(UNI) Appealed affected assessment" (after BR on x_uno57_student_ap_affected_assessments, fires on stateCHANGESTO8) also calls parent.update() unguarded. We tested the 3-BR fix in combination with this BR left unfixed and could not reproduce the loop on a single affected-assessment test case, though we haven't been able to fully replicate the original production scenario (closed application with multiple linked affected assessments).

Given item 2 also calls .update() unguarded on the same tables, even though we haven't reproduced an active loop through these specific paths, would you recommend applying setWorkflow(false) to this BR as a precaution as well?

Ideally we should use setWorkflow(false)  when we know there is no further business rules that need to run for the update that is being done. Although looking at "(UNI) Appealed affected assessment", I see the update might need to cascade upwards.

For example: The Application task, updates the parent record with this BR. If the parent record is also an application task, that may also need to update its parent task. If this is a valid use case in your scenario, then you may need to keep this BR as is.

If the above scenario is not valid for you. Which means, an Application task [x_uno57_student_ap_affected_assessments] record is never expected to have another application task as the parent OR you do not want more than one level of parent record to be updated by this BR, then you can add the setWorkflow(false)  here.

Another thing to consider is you are potentially updating state and assigned_to fields with this BR. So, if there are other BRs that need to trigger when any of these two fields are updated, then you cannot add the setWorkflow(false) on this BR.

main.Subject: AIS Index Event queue is not writable
main.Description: CRITICAL AIS Index Event queue is not writable.
main.Resolution notes:
Thanks for the confirmation Mithun. When there are more than 1 million events in the ais_index queue waiting to be processed, and the AIS Index Event Processor has not processed any events for a certain period of time, it will change the system property [glide.ais_event_queue_writable] OR [glide.ais.update_event_queue_writable] to "false", and generates an internal alert on the instance, which will create a case. The reasons behind this happening are multiple and not always evident. AI Search usually does not require any configuration or performance considerations. Simply turn it on, and it should 'just work.' The trouble is that when additional or custom tables are added as index sources. The default behavior may not be best depending on the source. By default, AI Search indexes all fields/columns for the table in the Indexed Source. This can make it easy to add new content to AI Search and quickly iterate on what works best. There are two things that should be considered, though, when configuring an Indexed Source: 1 Always map something to the text and title fields. This ensures that out-of-the-box functionality for result rendering and relevancy works consistently. 2 Make fields not relevant to search as 'no_text_index' in the Indexed Source. I will place this case in a solution state for now. Please accept the solution if no further questions arise; otherwise, please let us know, and we will be more than glad to assist. Best Regards. main.Resolution notes:
Hello Ashraf, We are placing this case in a Solution Proposed state as we have provided guidance regarding the Event Queue backlog. AFFECTED INSTANCES: SNC Instance - khcprod. ISSUE: An Instance Observer alert was triggered on the khcprod instance due to a continuous increase in the Event Queue backlog (sysevent table). The backlog exceeded 40,000 events for more than 15 minutes and was steadily increasing, indicating that event processing was not keeping up with event generation. SOLUTION PROPOSED: ServiceNow engineers investigated and identified that the Event Queue backlog was caused by a large influx of `ais_index` events, with over 334,000 unprocessed events in that specific queue. The investigation revealed that the majority of these events originated from frequent insert and update operations on the `sam_sw_product_lifecycle` table. While the `AIS Index Event Processor` job is successfully processing events, the generation rate is higher than the processing rate, leading to the backlog. NEXT STEPS: To mitigate the high volume of `ais_index` events, we recommend analyzing the columns on the `sam_sw_product_lifecycle` table that are triggering these updates. If certain columns are not required for AI Search, you can disable indexing for them by setting the dictionary attribute `no_text_index` to `true`. main.Subject: AI Search Results are not relevant in the Portal.
main.Description:
Hello Team,

The AI Search Results are not relevant to the query. 
For Example: If I search as "My Laptop is not working"
I get correct answer in the Genius Results Section but in the Search Results we get irrelevant Knowledge Articles. 

Is there a way to improve the results and also show relevant knowledge, Catalog Items?
main.Resolution notes:
Hello Nayani,

My name is Aleli, I'm one of the Subject Matter Experts of AI Search in ServiceNow. Looking to provide context to this behavior you are experiencing.

In ServiceNow, AI Search is an intelligent search engine that improves on traditional keyword search by using AI, machine learning, and relevance tuning.

Here's how it works at a high level:

--A) Table: Indexing

AI Search continuously indexes data from selected tables such as:

Knowledge articles
Catalog items
Incidents


--B) Query Understanding

When a user searches, AI Search:

Analyzes the search phrase
Handles misspellings and typos
Understands synonyms
Uses stemming (e.g., "running" → "run")
Interprets natural language queries

Example:

User searches: "can't connect to VPN"
AI Search may also look for articles containing:
remote access
VPN issue
network connection problem
3. Relevance Ranking

--C) Results are ranked using factors such as:

Keyword matches
User behavior (what users clicked before)
Freshness of content
Popularity of articles
Search profiles and boosts configured by admins

A highly viewed article about VPN issues may rank above a newer article with fewer views.

--D)  Search Profiles

Admins configure Search Profiles that determine:

Which tables are searched
Result ordering
Boosting rules
Facets and filters
Security restrictions

Different portals can use different search profiles.

The results that you are seeing is highly dependent on what is configured for the Search Source in a Search Profile

DOCS:
Search Source: (What is being searched)
https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/zurich/platform-administration/ai-search/search-sources-ais.html

Search Profile: Contains settings of what is being search in the Service Portal
https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/zurich/platform-administration/ai-search/defining-search-profiles-ais.html

The results are mainly calculated based off what is described above. So, in theory, those would be closest match. BUT if you want certain kb article to appear first, you can set up result improvement rules to boost certain kb articles / catalogs you wish to be seen first.


https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/zurich/platform-administration/ai-search/result-improvement-rules-ais.html


Hope this information helps and let us know if you would like to set up a call to discuss further


Best regards,

main.Resolution notes:
Hello Anusha,

We are placing this case in a Solution Proposed state as we have provided guidance regarding the functionality of the requested system properties.

AFFECTED INSTANCES: SNC Instance - eymyhrsand1.

ISSUE: After an upgrade to Australia Patch 3 HF1, certain system properties were observed in skipped logs being updated from 'true' to 'false'. A request was made to understand the functionality of the properties 'sn_ais_assist.dpr_ingestion_completed' and 'sn_ais_assist.passage_format_ingestion_completed', their default values, and the impact of them being disabled.

SOLUTION PROPOSED: The system properties 'sn_ais_assist.dpr_ingestion_completed' and 'sn_ais_assist.passage_format_ingestion_completed' are used to control the behavior of semantic search requests. Their default value is 'false'. They are intended to be set to 'true' automatically after semantic ingestion is completed. If these properties are disabled (set to 'false'), Now Assist in AI Search (multi-content response genius results) will not work as expected. The property 'sn_ais_assist.dpr_ingestion_completed' is a maintenance-only property, meaning it can typically only be updated by ServiceNow. Please see KB2690123 and KB2761945 for reference.

NEXT STEPS: If the property 'sn_ais_assist.dpr_ingestion_completed' needs to be enabled, you can run the following background script in the 'global' scope to set the value to 'true': 

gs.setProperty('sn_ais_assist.dpr_ingestion_completed', 'true');

var gr = new GlideRecord('sys_update_xml');

main.Description:
Newly published KBs cannot be found on portals in the prod environment only. I was able to publish KBs in sub-prod and kbs can be found instantly on the portals.

I published this KB on Friday after reindex was complete and as of today it cannot be found. You can try by going to the

main.Resolution notes:
Hello Maggie,

Thank you for your patience as we investigated this critical issue. 
We are placing this case in a Solution Proposed state as the root cause has been identified and a resolution implemented.

AFFECTED INSTANCES: SNC Instance - itsmnow.

ISSUE: Following a previous incident (CS9379853), newly published or retired Knowledge Base (KB) articles were not being reflected in the AI Search results on the production portal (mytech). The issue was specific to the production environment, as changes were appearing instantly in sub-production. This meant that critical, time-sensitive information was not accessible to users, and outdated information remained searchable, impacting over 1,000 users. For example, newly published articles like KB0320317, KB0320456, KB0320459, and KB0320483 were not found, while retired articles like KB0320284 and KB0320202 were still appearing in search results.

SOLUTION PROPOSED: 

ServiceNow engineers investigated and identified that the AI Search event queue was not processing updates for Knowledge Base articles. 

The root cause was determined to be the `sys_view_count` field on KB articles triggering an excessive number of indexing events, which caused the event queue to reach its processing limit. 

The system automatically set the property `glide.ais.update_event_queue_writable` to `false` to protect itself, which stopped all further indexing of KB articles. 

To resolve this, our internal development team first created a `no_text_index` for the `sys_view_count` and `use_count` fields to prevent them from triggering indexing events so frequently. 

They then reset the `glide.ais.update_event_queue_writable` property to `true`. This allowed the event queue to resume processing, and newly published and retired articles are now being correctly indexed by AI Search. A defect (PRB2052684) has been created to address the underlying product behavior, and you will receive notification as it progresses.

NEXT STEPS: 
The fix has been applied and confirmed to be working. No further action is required from your side.
You are welcome to keep this case open for a few days, should the issue reoccur, please REJECT the solution so our teams will follow up accordingly.

Please let me know if you have any questions by updating this case.

Best regards,

main.Subject: Not working AI Search on External Links
main.Description:
Problem Statement
We have configured AI Search to index external links by creating an Indexed Source for the external link records, creating a corresponding Search Source, and adding it to the CSM Portal Search Profile. AI Search is enabled on the CSM Portal.
The expected behaviour is that when a user clicks an external link search result, they should be redirected to the URL stored in the external link record.
Issue
Instead of redirecting users to the configured external URL, the search result redirects to the backend record (External Link record) in ServiceNow.
Investigation Performed
We investigated the issue and followed the configuration steps provided in the following ServiceNow Knowledge Base article:
KB: AI Search results how to navigate to external content or site - Support and Troubleshooting - Now Support
As recommended in the article, we also completed the required EVAM configuration. However, the issue still persists, and clicking the search result continues to open the backend record instead of the external URL.
Since the recommended configuration has not resolved the problem, we need ServiceNow Support to investigate and advise on the root cause or any additional configuration or fix required.
main.Resolution notes:
Hello Anatoliy,

Thank you for your patience while I investigated this issue.

Based on my testing, I found that the issue is caused by the configuration of the **CSM and CSP Portal Search Bundle**.

The current predicate bundle being used is:

https://unicefdev.service-now.com/sys_ux_composite_data_template_predicate_bundle.do?sys_id=2615e20cc3122010a6f3f97c9840dd94

During my investigation, I added the **External Links** predicate to this bundle and created the corresponding predicate record:

https://unicefdev.service-now.com/sys_ux_composite_data_template_predicate.do?sys_id=091a2fe03b168f50397638a693e45aa5&sysparm_record_target=sys_ux_composite_data_template_predicate&sysparm_record_row=2&sysparm_record_rows=2&sysparm_record_list=predicate_bundle%3D2615e20cc3122010a6f3f97c9840dd94%5EORDERBYorder

After making this configuration change, I verified that the External Link search results behave as expected and correctly redirect users to the configured external URL instead of opening the backend External Link record.

**Root Cause**

The **External Links predicate** was not included in the **CSM and CSP Portal Search Bundle**. Because of this, AI Search did not use the external navigation configuration and instead defaulted to opening the underlying ServiceNow record.

Adding the External Links predicate to the predicate bundle resolves the issue by enabling the expected external URL navigation.

Could you please verify the behavior from your end and let me know if the issue is now resolved?

Thank you for your time and cooperation throughout the investigation. If you have any questions or require any further assistance, please let me know and I will be happy to help.

main.Subject: LOS AI Search External Content not shown in AI Search
main.Description:
Hello,
we cloned our prod. instance some weeks ago.
We are using several external content connectors. They still working on the prod., training and test instance.
On dev the results are not show anymore in the ESC nor in the search preview tool.

Br
Leonard
main.Resolution notes:
Hello Leonard,

Thank you for your time on the call to discuss this issue. We are placing this case in a Solution Proposed state as the root cause has been identified and a resolution recommended.

AFFECTED INSTANCES: SNC Instance - serviceschwarzdev.

ISSUE: After a recent clone of the production instance, AI Search results for several external content connectors (initially reported as Google Drive, SAP SF, LeanIX, Cloud Storage, and ARIS) were no longer appearing for end-users in the dev instance's Employee Center (ESC) or the search preview tool. This issue was blocking all AI Search development and testing on the dev instance.

SOLUTION PROPOSED: Investigation determined that the issue affected all external content connectors (XCCs) and was not specific to the Google connector. 

The root cause was identified as a by-design Zero Trust Access (ZTA) control implemented on the search sources. This control uses a dynamic filter condition, `javascript:new global.SDS_NA_LOS_AIS_ZeroTrust().apply('https','forbidden')`, which is intended to suppress XCC content for any user who does not pass the ZTA check. 

The check requires users to have the "sn_hr_sp.hrsp_employee" role. 

Users without this role were being correctly filtered from seeing external content search results, which is the intended behavior of the ZTA design. 

The issue was not related to ACLs, namespaces, or user-mapping. 

The resolution is to grant the "sn_hr_sp.hrsp_employee" role to any end-user who should be entitled to see search results from the external content connectors.

NEXT STEPS: To resolve this for affected users, please ensure they are granted the "sn_hr_sp.hrsp_employee" role. 

Users who should not have access to external content are being correctly filtered by the existing design.

Please let me know if you have any questions by updating this case.

Best regards,
Bhoomika Bisht

main.Description: Event Queue Performance
main.Resolution notes:
Hello Frank van Es,

We are placing this case in a Solution Proposed state.

AFFECTED INSTANCES:
devolksbank

ISSUE:
System Event Queue Impact – Delay in Processing (Email, Text Indexing and/or Flow Events).

SOLUTION PROPOSED:
Firstly, thank you for reaching out to ServiceNow support.

We have reviewed your issue.

Upon looking further into the issue, we can see that the heavy influx of events is due to certain tables. I have attached its details down below.
You can mark the unused fields in AI Search with attribute "no_text_index" = "true", post which the fields won't get indexed, significantly reducing the AIS event queue

+------+--------------------+--------------------------+-------+---------+
| Port | name | table | state | count |
+------+--------------------+--------------------------+-------+---------+
| 3325 | ais_index | sam_sw_product_lifecycle | ready | 1123650 |

Please refer to the following doc to add no_text_index attribute in the indexed source.
https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/zurich/platform-administration/ai-search/field-settings-list-ais.html

Whenever there are bulk updates made on a table, many events get triggered in the sysevent table for the data to index to the AIS database. This will cause a delay in processing the records for the AIS database. In order to control the events that are getting generated, you can add a few columns that you don't want to index to the 'no_text_index' attribute

Steps to add no_text_index
>> Navigate to the Indexed source and open the record for any table
>> In the 'Field settings and mappings'
>> Click on new and add the attribute "No_text_index" and in the column add the desired column

To help address your query, we kindly recommend discussing this with your internal team to identify which fields would be appropriate for applying the "No_text_index" configuration, as we may not have complete visibility into your specific business requirements or use case.

main.Subject: Urgent: Performance Alert – Multiple Node Restarts Detected Due To Out-Of-Memory Errors
main.Description: Multiple Out Of Memory errors detected
main.Resolution notes:
Hello Pramod/ Divya,

Thank you for your time on the calls to discuss this case. We are placing this case in a Solution Proposed state as the root cause has been identified and a resolution has been provided.

AFFECTED INSTANCES: daimlertruck.

ISSUE: The instance experienced multiple Out-of-Memory (OOM) errors, leading to node restarts. The performance degradation was triggered by a system alert for "Multiple Node Restarts Detected Due To Out-Of-Memory Errors".

SOLUTION PROPOSED: ServiceNow engineers investigated and identified that the Out-of-Memory errors and subsequent node restarts were caused by the "AIS Index Event Processor" job consuming excessive memory. This was due to the job processing approximately 6.1 million orphaned records in the List Elements (`sys_ui_list_element`) table where the `list_id` field was null. These records were created approximately three years ago. Due to data retention limitations (binlogs are only available for 3 days), the exact source of the record creation could not be determined.

The recommended solution is to clean up these orphaned records by either archiving or truncating them, as detailed in Knowledge Base article KB1699445. This will prevent the "AIS Index Event Processor" from consuming excessive memory and resolve the performance issue.

During our calls, we discussed the customer's inability to create an archive rule for the `sys_ui_list_element` table, as it was not visible in their UI. While this functionality worked for the support engineer (including when impersonating the customer's user), we confirmed that support engineers are not permitted to create archival rules on a customer's behalf. The issue preventing the customer from seeing the table is likely related to user permissions on their side.

NEXT STEPS: Please follow the guidance in KB1699445 to archive or remove the 6.1 million orphaned records from the `sys_ui_list_element` table where `list_id` is empty. You may also need to investigate internal permissions to allow your users to create the necessary archival rule for the "List Elements" (`sys_ui_list_element`) table.

Please let me know if you have any questions by updating this case.

Best regards,
Hanisha Cheruku

main.Resolution notes:
Hello Pete,

Thank you for your patience while I investigated this issue.

I have attached the relevant log to this case. Based on my review, I observed multiple occasions where the AI Search connection tests failed due to connection timeouts while attempting to communicate with the AI Search backend service. Specifically, the logs show repeated SearchConnectionTest failures with SocketTimeoutException: Connect timed out, preventing the instance from establishing a connection to the AI Search service during the affected timeframe.

Additionally, I found log entries indicating that the platform was temporarily unable to retrieve the AI Search partition health status due to connection failures with the backend service.

Since both search operations and partition health checks depend on communication with the AI Search backend, these failures indicate that the instance temporarily lost connectivity to the AI Search backend rather than encountering an issue with AI Search configuration, search profiles, indexing, or plugins.

As part of the investigation, I also verified whether any plugin repairs, updates, or configuration changes occurred during the affected timeframe and did not find any evidence of such changes. The logs likewise do not indicate any modifications to AI Search configuration or indexing. Furthermore, because the issue resolved without any manual intervention, the available evidence indicates that connectivity between the instance and the AI Search backend was automatically restored, allowing AI Search to resume normal operation.

Based on the available logs, the behavior is most consistent with a transient infrastructure connectivity issue affecting communication with the AI Search backend service rather than an issue with the instance configuration.

At this time, the issue is no longer occurring, and I am unable to reproduce the behavior. Since the logs do not indicate any persistent configuration issues and the service has recovered, there are no additional troubleshooting steps to perform at this time. If the issue recurs, please let log a new case so that we can troubleshoot effectively.

main.Subject: AI Search for Next Experience: Guidance on Attachment, Email, Activity Stream Indexing & Performance Impact
main.Description:
Performance Impact

* Are there any recommendations or limitations related to indexing large volumes of records and attachments?


Search Within Attachments and Inline Images

* Is it possible to search the content within attached documents (PDFs, Word files, etc.)?
* Can text embedded within inline images also be indexed and searched?


Email Searchability

* For emails generated or associated with these cases, can they be included in search results?
* If searching the entire email body is not supported, can at least the email subject be indexed and made searchable?


Activity Stream Content

* Can content from the Activity Stream, such as Additional Comments and Work Notes, be indexed and searchable through the Search Application?


Attachment Content Indexing

* When attachments are added to a case (whether inline images, documents, PDFs, etc.), can the search engine read and index the content within those attachments?
* If a keyword exists inside an attachment, will the corresponding case record be returned in the search results along with the relevant content reference?


We would appreciate your guidance on the above points, including any prerequisites, limitations, or best practices that should be considered.
main.Resolution notes:
[code]

Hello Amey,


We are moving your case to Solution Proposed as we believe the information provided below will resolve your issue. If we have addressed your concerns, you may accept the solution to close this case or reject the solution if it does not answer the original question raised with this ticket. At any time in the Solution Proposed state, you may add additional questions or updates.


Request: 

AI Search for Next Experience: Guidance on Attachment, Email, Activity Stream Indexing & Performance Impact


Solution Proposed: 

​1. Performance Impact

1.1 Are there any recommendations or limitations related to indexing large volumes of records and attachments?

Yes.

  • AI Search is designed to support large data sets, but indexing volume directly impacts indexing duration, storage consumption, and search infrastructure utilisation. 
  • Attachments can significantly increase index size and processing requirements because AI Search extracts and indexes attachment content in addition to record data. 
  • For attachment indexing:
    • Maximum supported attachment size is25 MB.
    • Traditional keyword indexing processes approximately the first1 MB of extracted text.
    • Larger documents may require semantic indexing/search capabilities to fully leverage their content. 
  • Best practice is to carefully scope indexed sources and only index data that provides business value for search. AI Search supports indexed source filtering, retention policies, and field-level controls to help manage index size.


2. Search Within Attachments and Inline Images

2.1. Is it possible to search the content within attached documents (PDFs, Word files, etc.)?

Yes.

AI Search can index content from supported attachment types when attachment indexing is enabled for the indexed source. Supported formats include:

  • PDF (with searchable text)
  • Microsoft Word (.doc, .docx)
  • Microsoft Excel (.xls, .xlsx)
  • Microsoft PowerPoint (.ppt, .pptx)
  • HTML
  • Text files and several other common document formats. 

If a keyword exists within the extracted content of one of these attachments, the parent record can be returned in search results. 


2.2. Can text embedded within inline images also be indexed and searched?

Generally, only text that can be extracted from the attachment is indexed.

  • PDFs containing selectable/searchable text are supported. 
  • The documentation does not state that AI Search performs Optical Character Recognition (OCR) on images or screenshots embedded within records, emails, or attachments. Based on the available documentation, text that exists only as pixels within an image should not be assumed to be searchable.

Therefore, searchable text content is supported, but OCR-based extraction from inline images is not documented as a supported capability.


3. Email Searchability

3.1 For emails generated or associated with these cases, can they be included in search results?

This depends on how the search solution is configured.

  • AI Search indexes configured tables and indexed sources. 
  • Internal AI Search discussions note that indexing thesys_emailtable is not generally available as a standard AI Search use case and has been identified as a separate capability/roadmap consideration in some projects. 

Therefore, email searchability should be validated against the specific implementation and indexed sources being used.


3.1 If searching the entire email body is not supported, can at least the email subject be indexed and made searchable?

Yes, if the email table is being indexed.

AI Search allows administrators to configure which fields from an indexed source are searchable. If email records are configured as an indexed source, fields such as the subject can be indexed and searched. 


4. Activity Stream Content

4.1 Can content from the Activity Stream, such as Additional Comments and Work Notes, be indexed and searchable through the Search Application?

Potentially yes, but it requires configuration.

  • AI Search indexes data from configured tables and fields.
  • Journal fields can be included in AI Search and related AI Search/RAG configurations. Internal guidance references support for indexing journal-field content and related record information. 

Because Additional Comments and Work Notes are stored as journal activity rather than standard string fields, customers should validate whether those journal fields are included in the indexed source configuration for the target table.


5. Attachment Content Indexing

5.1 When attachments are added to a case (whether inline images, documents, PDFs, etc.), can the search engine read and index the content within those attachments?

Yes, provided:

  • Attachment indexing is enabled on the indexed source.
  • The attachment format is supported.
  • The attachment is not encrypted.
  • The attachment content can be extracted by AI Search. 

For encrypted files, AI Search indexes metadata only and does not extract searchable content. 


5.2 If a keyword exists inside an attachment, will the corresponding case record be returned in the search results along with the relevant content reference?

Yes.

When attachment indexing is enabled, AI Search indexes attachment content associated with the parent record. Searches can match text extracted from the attachment, allowing the related case/record to be returned as a result. 


Key Prerequisites and Best Practices

  • Configure the case table as an AI Search indexed source. 
  • Enableindex_attachmentsfor the indexed source if attachment content should be searchable. 
  • Reindex the source after enabling attachment indexing. 
  • Restrict indexed fields to content that provides business value to reduce index size and improve performance. 
  • Validate journal-field (Work Notes / Additional Comments) indexing requirements during implementation.
  • Do not assume OCR support for text contained only within images unless separately validated for the specific release and implementation.


Next Steps:

Hello Hardik,

I tried calling you today in your provided contact number but the calls went unanswered.
We are moving your case to Solution Proposed as we believe the information provided below will resolve your issue. If you have any queries, please let me know on the case, and I will schedule a zoom meeting and explain you the details.

Issue:
The custom AI Search Profile was not returning any search results when executed via script, whereas the out-of-the-box (OOB) search profile was working as expected.

Most Probable Cause:
The AI Search Indexed Source configuration was missing required attribute mapping for the dot-walking reference fields(e.g. dot-walking field assignment_group.name has been used in 'Search Source' filter but was not configured in Indexed Source attribute which is mandatory, and also mentioned in our Prod Doc).
Without this attribute enabled, searches referencing child fields on reference records fail to return results.

Solution Proposed:
We updated the target Indexed Source configuration to enable dot-walking for reference fields:

  • Navigated to AI Search > Indexing > Indexed Sources.
  • Opened the relevant Indexed Source record for the target table (e.g., Incident).
  • Under the Attributes related list, configured the following:
    Indexed Source: Target Indexed Source
    Field: assignment_group (reference field name on the parent table)
    Attribute: dot_walk_fields
    Value: name (target field name on the referenced sys_user_group table)

https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/ai-search/enable-ref-table-field-index-ais.html

  • Saved and re-indexed as required.

For additional details on this process, please refer to the product documentation on Enabling reference table field index for AI Search.

Testing Performed:
After applying the dot_walk_fields configuration, we re-indexed the incident Indexed Source, tested the search profile both from Search Preview and via script, and verified that search results are now successfully returned as expected.

main.Description:

**English follows Japanese
お世話になっております。
Knowledge ManagementのKnowledge CenterにおけるAI Searchの検索仕様について、現在検証を進めており、仕様の理解を明確にするためお問い合わせいたしました。
Knowledge記事の検索性向上を目的として検証を行っておりますが、検索アルゴリズムおよび優先順位付けについて、以下の点をご確認させてください。

1. ナレッジ記事[kb_knowledge]テーブルに存在するメタフィールド[Meta]とText search weightの影響について

　＜当方認識＞
　Metaフィールドは検索対象として利用される
　Text search weight の値により検索順位が変動する
　デフォルト値は以下の通り

　設定なし：1
　番号：30
　簡単な説明：10
　メタ：10

　→このため、検索順位は
　「番号」＞「簡単な説明」＝「メタ」
　となる認識です
　また、MetaのText search weightを最大に設定した場合、当該キーワードを含む記事が優先的に上位表示される認識です。

　＜確認事項＞
　上記認識に相違はありませんでしょうか。検索順位は関連性が高い順で表示される認識ですが、Text search weight の値によって関連性は変動するのでしょうか。
　Text search weightはZing検索向けの仕様と理解しておりますが、AI Searchにおいても加味されるのでしょうか

　参考：
　Set the relative weight of a field（https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/search-administration/t_ControlMatchRelevanceByField.html）

2. 日本語検索における形態素解析について
　＜当方認識＞
　AI Searchでは、日本語検索時に形態素解析（単語分割）は行われない
　例：
　「ドコモマックス」検索時に
　「ドコモ」「マックス」に分割されて検索されることはない
　＜確認事項＞
　上記認識に相違はありませんでしょうか

3. 各種検索設定の適用範囲について
　＜当方認識＞
　■Zing検索のみで適用可能
　同義語ディクショナリ（ts_synonym_dictionary）
　日本語ユーザートークン（ts_japanese_token_dictionary）
　ストップワード（ts_stop）

■AI Searchのみで適用可能
　AI検索ディクショナリ（ais_dictionary）
　→同義語・ストップワード機能を含む

　参考：https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/ja-JP/platform-administration/ai-search/dictionary-form-ais.html
　＜確認事項＞
　上記認識に相違はありませんでしょうか

4. AI Searchの検索仕様に関する公開情報
　Knowledge Centerで使用されるAI Searchにおいて、以下に関する公開ドキュメントやベストプラクティスがあればご教示ください。

　・検索アルゴリズム
　・スコアリングロジック
　・検索結果の表示順制御
---
Thank you for your continued support.
We are currently conducting tests on the search specifications for AI Search in the Knowledge Center of Knowledge Management, and we are reaching out to clarify our understanding of these specifications.
We are conducting these tests to improve the searchability of knowledge articles, and we would like to confirm the following points regarding the search algorithm and prioritization.

1. The impact of the [Meta] meta field in the knowledge article [kb_knowledge] table and the “Text search weight”

　<Our Understanding>
　The Meta field is used as a search target.
　Search rankings vary depending on the value of the “Text search weight.”
　The default values are as follows:

　No setting: 1
　Number: 30
　Short description: 10
　Meta: 10

　→ Therefore, our understanding is that the search ranking is:
　“Number” > “Short description” = “Meta”
　
　Additionally, we understand that setting the “Meta” Text Search Weight to the maximum causes articles containing that keyword to be displayed higher in the search results.

　<Points for Confirmation>
　Is there any discrepancy with the understanding stated above? We understand that search rankings are displayed in order of relevance, but does this relevance vary depending on the Text Search Weight value?
　We understand that Text Search Weight is a specification for Zing Search, but is it also taken into account in AI Search?

　Reference:
　Set the relative weight of a field (https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/search-administration/t_ControlMatchRelevanceByField.html)

2. Morphological Analysis in Japanese Searches
　<Our Understanding>
　In AI Search, morphological analysis (word segmentation) is not performed during Japanese searches.
　Example:
　When searching for “Docomo Max,”
　the search is not split into “Docomo” and “Max”
　<Points to Confirm>
　Is there any discrepancy with the understanding stated above?

3. Scope of Application for Various Search Settings
　<Our Understanding>
　■ Applicable only to Zing Search
　Synonym dictionary (ts_synonym_dictionary)
　Japanese user token dictionary (ts_japanese_token_dictionary)
　Stop words(ts_stop)

■ Applicable only to AI Search
　AI Search dictionary (ais_dictionary)
　→ Includes synonym and stopword functionality

　Reference: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/ja-JP/platform-administration/ai-search/dictionary-form-ais.html
　<Points to Confirm>
　Is there any discrepancy with the understanding above?

4. Public Information Regarding AI Search Specifications
　Please let us know if there are any public documents or best practices regarding the following aspects of the AI Search used in the Knowledge Center:

　・Search algorithm
　・Scoring logic
　・Control over the display order of search results

main.Description:
Hello,

We are experiencing inconsistent search behavior when using the global search configured with AI Search.

When a user searches for a word or reference that is present only in the Work Notes of a Requested Item (RITM), the RITM is not returned in the global search results.

The same search works correctly for other task-based records. For example, when the searched word is present in the Work Notes of an Incident or a Story, the corresponding record is returned as expected.

We also confirmed that the Work Notes content of the RITM is searchable through the standard list search.
- Open the list of Requested Items.

- The expected RITM is returned.

The issue therefore appears to be limited to AI Search and specifically to Work Notes on Requested Items.

main.Resolution notes: Hello Alain, We are placing this case in a Close state as you have confirmed the fix is working correctly in your environment. [code]AFFECTED INSTANCES:[/code] valais, valaisdev, valaistest. [code]ISSUE:[/code] AI Search / global search did not return Requested Items (RITMs) when the search term was present only in the Work Notes field, even though the same term was returned correctly via standard list/keyword search. [code]SOLUTION PROPOSED: [/code] ServiceNow engineers investigated and identified that the sc_req_item.work_notes field was protected by a scripted field-level ACL. AI Search does not support scripted field-level ACLs, so when a field is guarded by one, AI Search silently excludes it from indexing and search results, even though the field remains searchable through the platform's standard keyword search (which evaluates security differently). ServiceNow recommended adding a new non-scripted read ACL on the sc_req_item.work_notes field, allowing AI Search to index and return work_notes content while existing scripted ACLs continue to enforce your security policies on the platform itself. You implemented this change and confirmed RITMs are now correctly returned in AI Search when the search term is present in Work Notes. [code]NEXT STEPS:[/code] No further action is needed at this time. If you have other fields on this or other tables that are protected by scripted ACLs and need to be searchable via AI Search, the same approach (adding a non-scripted read ACL) can be applied. If historical work notes still don't appear in search, a full re-index of the sc_req_item table may be needed — please let me know and I'm happy to assist. I'm really glad we were able to get to the bottom of this and that the fix is working well for your team. Thank you for your patience throughout the investigation. Please let me know if you have any questions by updating this case. Best Regards, [code]Juan Pablo Gómez[/code] [code]Technical Support Engineer[/code] 8am - 5pm US Eastern | Monday - Friday

main.Subject: AI-Searchの制御の仕方について質問
main.Description:
Now support ご担当者様

いつもお世話になっております。
NRIの相澤と申します。
件名の通り、AI-Searchの制御の仕方について疑問があり、ご回答をいただきたく存じます。

【やりたいこと】
特定の権限を持つユーザー（例：特定のロールを持っている、特定のグループに所属している、等）のみ、AI-Searchを使用できるようにしたい

【私の理解】
AI-Searchではなく、通常のService Portal 検索ソース（sp_search_source）では、関連リストよりUser Criteria（ユーザー条件）の設定ができ、こちらで特定のグループの選択ができる認識です。
しかし、AI Search の検索ソース（sys_ais_search_source）では関連リストが設定できず、類似するアクセスコントロール機能もないように見受けられました。
そのため、
・Service Portal 検索ソース（sp_search_source）では【やりたいこと】の制御ができる
・AI Search の検索ソース（sys_ais_search_source）では【やりたいこと】の制御ができない
と理解しております。

【お伺いしたいこと】
・【私の理解】があっていれば、AI Searchを使用できるユーザーを設定することはできないことになりますが、認識は合っておりますでしょうか？
・認識があっている場合、【やりたいこと】を実現できる類似の制御機能はありますか？あれば設定方法をご教示いただきたいです。
・認識があっていない場合、どこでどのような設定をすれば【やりたいこと】を実現できるかご教示いただきたいです。

【参考】
・画像１枚目：AI Search の検索ソース（sys_ais_search_source）の設定画面までの行き方
・画像２枚目：AI Search の検索ソース（sys_ais_search_source）の設定画面を開いたところ

お手数をおかけしますが、ご教示よろしくお願いいたします。

main.Subject: System Event Queue Impact – Delay in Processing (Email, Text Indexing and/or Flow Events)
main.Description: Event Queue Performance
main.Resolution notes:
Hello Aparna,

We are placing this case in a Solution Proposed state as our engineering analysis is complete and the event queue is currently processing normally, with a configuration change recommended to prevent recurrence.

AFFECTED INSTANCES: agl.

ISSUE: The ais_index system event queue on instance agl built up a significant backlog (peaking at over 6.8 million ready events), causing delays in processing that could impact email, text indexing, and flow executions.

SOLUTION PROPOSED: 
- ServiceNow engineers investigated and identified that the backlog was driven almost entirely by a high volume of ais_index insert events generated against a small set of Software Asset Management and Hardware Asset Management tables/fields that are indexed for AI Search but not used in search relevancy. As of the latest check, the queue has recovered and is processing normally (ais_index size/processed counts are stable, e.g. 320 queued / 1,779 processed as of 2026-07-27 19:21 UTC).
- ServiceNow recommends the customer apply the no_text_index attribute to the following data source fields to stop these high-churn, non-search-relevant fields from generating unnecessary indexing events and provide lasting relief:
- samp_sw_product_definition: entitlement_definition, product_type, sys_domain, license_metric, publisher_part_number
- sn_hamp_lifecycle_definition: active, content_version, lifecycle_phase, hw_product_model, start_date
- sam_sw_product_lifecycle: active, content_version, lifecycle_phase, hw_product_model, start_date
- sn_hamp_hw_product_model: model_number, stage_energy_star, energy_star, epeat_compliant, name, stage_epeat_compliant, hw_product

NEXT STEPS: 
- Please have your ServiceNow admin apply the no_text_index attribute to the fields listed above via the AI Search data source configuration (referencing KB1527656 for detailed steps). This should be done at your earliest convenience to prevent the ais_index queue from building up again during future large data syncs/imports on these tables. We will continue to monitor the queue on our end in the interim.

Please let me know if you have any questions by updating this case.

Best regards,
Danny Romero

main.Subject: System Event Queue Impact – Delay in Processing (Email, Text Indexing and/or Flow Events)
main.Description: Event Queue Performance
main.Resolution notes:
Hello Ashraf,

My name is Yaser and I have taken the case over to assist. Please find the summary below.

AFFECTED INSTANCES: khcprod

ISSUE: sysevent getting full of ais_index events.

CAUSE: Product defect: PRB2010143.

During content updates in the ITAM Content Library, a large number of ais_index events are generated for the sam_sw_product_lifecycle (SAM software lifecycle) and sn_hamp_lifecycle_definition (HAM hardware lifecycle) tables. These events appear in the Event Log (All > System Logs > Events, sysevent table).

The excessive events are triggered because system metadata columns (sys_id, sys_class_name, sys_created_by, sys_created_on, sys_updated_by, sys_updated_on, sys_mod_count, sys_domain, sys_domain_path, sys_tags) on the AI Search datasources for these two tables are missing the no_text_index field attribute. Without this attribute, the AI Search indexing engine includes these columns in the vector index.

Since columns like sys_updated_on, sys_mod_count, and sys_updated_by change on every record write, each content update triggers re-indexing events for all affected records, flooding the AI Search indexing queue, causing indexing backlogs, and degrading AI Search performance — despite these columns carrying no semantic business value for content search.

SOLUTION PROPOSED: 
Thank you for your patience on this case. After further review, we can confirm that the issue is a product defect with ID PRB2010143. This issue has been fixed in the following ServiceNow release:

1. Zurich Patch 11
2. Australia Patch 4

We suggest scheduling an upgrade to at least Zurich Patch 11. After the upgrade, you will have to set the system property "glide.ais.update_event_queue_writable" back to true

Please let me know if you have any clarifications. While waiting for your update or response, we are now setting this case in Solution Proposed state. When you're ready or if you don't have any further concerns, please feel free to close the case by clicking Accept Solution.

Have a great day!

Best regards,
Yaser

ISSUE: Reindexing the Knowledge table, state "not started", Prod

This is affected by PRB2057650.

SOLUTION PROPOSED:

Root Cause:
In ServerIngestionService.uploadContent(), when LimitedSizeInputStream detects the size limit is exceeded mid-stream, an exception is thrown but the remaining bytes in the request InputStream are never consumed. 

When this happens, the sys_trigger "AIS Index Event Processor" stops processing events afterwards. As a workaround, we need to consistently repair the AIS Enabler plugin (which resets the sys_trigger and starts ingestion again).

main.Subject: AI Search custom search source results in Portal are rendering without clickable navigation links.
main.Description:
We have configured AI Search for Now Assist within our Portal. While genius results and standard search results are returning successfully, we are experiencing a rendering/routing issue with a specific custom search source (Delivery 2.0) for our custom table (x_gfnll_delivery_2_methodology).

When a user performs a search that yields results from this table, the EVAM card renders correctly with the Title and Overview, but the card itself is not clickable. There is no hyperlink or action bound to the card, preventing users from navigating to the actual record.
main.Resolution notes:
``` Hi Jared, I hope you're doing well! I'm moving this case to the Solution Proposed state while you review the resolution details below. [code]Description: [/code] Search results returned by the "Delivery 2.0" custom search source (table x_gfnll_delivery_2_methodology) were rendering the EVAM card correctly in the ESC Portal (title, icon, teaser), but the card title was not being wrapped in a clickable navigation anchor. As a result, end users could see the results but could not click through to open the actual record from the portal search UI. [code]Solution: [/code] The root cause was identified on the EVAM View Configuration record for the Delivery 2.0 search source. The associated View Template (sn-search-result-evam-card) was correctly mapping the card title to the AI Search teaser field ("title": "ai_search_teaser_title"), and the many-to-many binding to the "navigation" Declarative Action was in place. However, the "Custom Fields" list on the EVAM View Configuration was empty, so the AIS-provided fields referenced by the template (ai_search_teaser_title, ai_search_teaser_text, and related metadata fields) were not being exposed to the template at runtime. Because the title mapping could not resolve to a valid value, the sn-search-result-evam-card component fell back to rendering the title as plain text without wrapping it in a navigation anchor, leaving the card visually complete but non-clickable. To resolve the issue, the following Custom Fields were added to the EVAM View Configuration for the Delivery 2.0 search source, matching the pattern used by the out-of-the-box Knowledge (kb_knowledge) view configuration in the same bundle: ai_search_teaser_title, ai_search_teaser_text, document_index, topics, child_docs After the change, the ESC Portal search results for the Delivery 2.0 source now render with a clickable title anchor and navigate correctly to the target record, matching the behavior of the Knowledge results in the same search profile. [code]Applicable Versions: [/code] All supported ServiceNow releases where AI Search for Service Portal and EVAM (Entity View Action Mapper) are used with a custom-table search source and the sn-search-result-evam-card component. This is a configuration-level correction and is not tied to a specific patch or PRB. If successful, you can proceed with implementing the change in the production environment. We have around 918K incidents created in last 3 years but it only indexed 587008 records (https://synopsysqa.service-now.com/nav_to.do?uri=ais_ingest_datasource_stats.do?sys_id=66daa5521bcacfd0c152ec63604bcba5). Why?

FYI. I re-initiate the indexing again.
main.Resolution notes:
Hi Xiaoming,

Thank you for your patience, and apologies for the delay in response.
We have now received confirmation from our Dev team on this issue.

ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED:
>> The Incident indexed source originally had a 2-year (730-day) OOB retention policy. When it was set to 2 years, the Guard Rail Limit for Indexed Data Sources calculated and stored a Max Retention Days value of 730 days for the Incident data source. When you later updated the retention policy to 3 years (1095 days), this guardrail value was not automatically recalculated — so indexing continued to be capped at 730 days behind the scenes, which is why only ~587K–721K of the eligible records were indexed instead of the full set on your QA instance and totally 721399 records were indexed out of over 1 million records in Incident table in your Dev instance.

>> Please be informed that, our Dev team has now logged a new problem record/system bug - PRB2074141 to address this gap (guardrail not auto-recalculating on retention policy change) in a future release. We have now linked this problem - PRB2074141 to this case for your reference, so that you can be notified automatically once this problem is investigated and fixed.
 
WORKAROUND (to apply now on your Dev instance/QA instance):

1- Delete the Incident table entry in the ais_guard_rail_limit_data_source table.
2- Trigger the "AIS Index Purge Stale Document" scheduled job to force the guardrail value to recalculate.
3- Re-check the Incident entry in ais_guard_rail_limit_data_source to confirm the Max Retention Days value now correctly updated and shows 1095.
4- Once confirmed, you can re-index as needed, since the earlier configuration change meant proper indexing didn't occur— it should now pick up the full 3-year record set.

Kindly try above workaround steps and please let us know if that works fine for you.

Next Steps :
Thank you for contacting ServiceNow Technical Support and we look forward to working with you in the future !
Based on the information provided and current status of this case, we are moving it to Solution Proposed state. Kindly, let me know if you have any further questions on it. 

Best Regards,

main.Description:
Hi,
We are seeing some unexpected AI Search behaviour in Employee Center and would like to get some guidance on the AI search behaviour.

[image_1.png]

[image_4.png]
[image_5.png]
