main.Subject: Indexing of Knowledge and Catalog Items Failing at Critical Service Cutover Time
main.Description: We seem to have several failures in Ai Search indexing affecting a critical service cutover - the implications are that new catalog items are not being surfaced, adn old knowledge answers are being surfaced in searches in ESC.  I have followed the 'Index All Tables' approach in the documentation and no luck.  We need to resolve whatever is blocking this ASAP.
main.Resolution notes:
Hello Chris,

Thank you for your patience as we worked to resolve this issue. We are placing this case in a Solution Proposed state as the root cause has been identified and a resolution implemented.

AFFECTED INSTANCES: SNC Instance - virginia.

ISSUE: AI Search indexing for Knowledge and Catalog Items was failing, causing a critical production impact where new items were not discoverable via search. The `ais_index` event queue was severely backlogged, growing to over 200,000 events, with zero events being processed. System logs showed persistent `AisUnavailableException` and `Connection reset by peer` errors, indicating a complete stall in the ingestion process.

SOLUTION PROPOSED: ServiceNow engineers investigated and identified that the AI Search indexing queue was completely stalled due to a known issue, tracked under problem record PRB1875924. The root cause was a record in the `x_uno61_osp_req_osp_requests` table containing an attachment larger than the 100 MB limit (approximately 178 MB). This oversized attachment caused the indexing job to fail and continuously retry, blocking the entire queue and preventing any new content from being indexed.

As a workaround, you excluded the problematic record by adding a filter condition to the corresponding Indexed Source (`ais_datasource` record `9d8914f41bb98a105bd61f87b04bcbd8`). Once this record was excluded, the `ais_index` event queue immediately began processing, and the backlog of over 200,000 events was successfully cleared. The problem record PRB1875924 has since been moved to a "Fixed" state. For more details on this issue, please refer to Knowledge Base article KB3137872.

Regarding the events in a "transferred" state, this is expected behavior during table rotation. These historical records are automatically cleaned up by a built-in process according to the table rotation policy and do not require manual deletion. Further details on this process can be found in Knowledge Base article KB0780216.

NEXT STEPS: All queued `ais_index` events have been processed, and indexing functionality has been restored. For details on the table rotation policy for "transferred" events, you may wish to raise a separate case with our performance team.

Please let me know if you have any questions by updating this case.

Enriching the Short Description improves the Search Results, but has no impact on the Suggested Results.
Adding the Meta field to the OOTB Catalog Item Indexed Source, then reindexing, also improves the Search Results, but still has no impact on the Suggested Results.
Suggested Results also behave differently depending on the environment and even between users who satisfy the same User Criteria.

According to the ServiceNow documentation, Suggested Results use a dedicated relevancy model based mainly on:
-Title matching
- Freshness

Another point that surprised me is that the Semantic Search Mappings only contain:

name → title
name → body
description → body
short_description is not mapped, yet updating it clearly improves the Search Results.

 Questions
1. What are the recommended best practices to improve Catalog Item discoverability (both in Suggested Results & Search Results) ? 
2. Is adding the Meta field to the OOTB Catalog Item Indexed Source considered a supported/recommended customization?
3. Could this have unintended impacts on other consumers such as Now Assist?
4. Is using Meta preferable to creating  Relevancy Improvement Rules?

6. Is there any supported way to improve Suggested Results beyond optimizing the Name/Title?
7. Is it expected that short_description improves Search Results even though it is not included in the Semantic Search Mappings, but is configured in the Field Settings & Mapping (map_to = text)? How is this field used by AI Search?

main.Description: Event Queue Performance
main.Resolution notes:
Hello Mayte,

We are placing this case in a Solution Proposed state as we have provided guidance to resolve the issue.

AFFECTED INSTANCES: ferrovial.

ISSUE: The instance experienced performance degradation due to delays in the System Event Queue, specifically affecting Email, Text Indexing, and/or Flow Events. This was caused by a large number of events in the `ais_index` queue.

SOLUTION PROPOSED: ServiceNow engineers investigated and identified that the event queue delay was caused by a large influx of `ais_index` events. This is a recurring issue related to a known problem (PRB1676568) where frequent updates to certain tables, such as `sn_vul_vulnerable_item` and `sn_query_gen_dimension`, generate an excessive number of AI Search indexing events. The events were indexing on the `sys_updated_on` field, which triggers re-indexing on every update.

To mitigate this and prevent future occurrences, we have provided the following recommendations as detailed in Knowledge Base article KB1442411:
1. Implement a "Set no_text_index field mapping for sys_user indexed source".
2. Update the "sort_by_date" setting to "sys_created_on" instead of "sys_updated_on" for the relevant index sources.

These changes will optimize the system by reducing the frequency of updates to the tables, thereby preventing the generation of excessive AIS index events.

main.Resolution notes:
Hi @[Sushmitha Bhari]

Based on the image, the user was not using a private browsing session, so browser caching could have been a contributing factor. I reviewed the users' logs for any outstanding transactions and did not identify anything indicating this is a server-side or ServiceNow platform issue, other than the session timing behavior that was previously shared.

We have tested and have not been able to reproduce the behavior on our end. As shared previously in the other case, the root cause appears to be related to the browser or VDI environment on the affected user's machine, rather than the ServiceNow platform or backend infrastructure.

Based on our investigation, the platform appears to be delivering the response correctly. However, processing and rendering a large volume of data on the client side may occasionally cause delays or unresponsiveness, especially if the browser or VDI session is constrained by memory, heap usage, cache, or browser extensions.

Currently, we are unable to proceed further from the ServiceNow side given the nature of the issue. Recommended actions for the affected users are:
1. Use an Incognito/Private browsing session with the latest version of Chrome or Edge to bypass potential extension conflicts. Based on the screenshot provided, the user was not using a private session.
2. Clear browser cache and cookies, and disable unnecessary browser extensions to free up browser resources.
3. Test from a non-VDI machine to rule out any VDI-related memory or heap constraints as a contributing factor.

If you would like to connect and set up a call to review the above, we would be more than happy to do so. Please let us know your availability.

For any additional concerns, we can also reach out to @Tiffany Crowder (NOW).

Hello Michael,

We are placing this case in a Solution Proposed state as the root cause has been identified, a permanent fix has been backported to the upcoming ZP12 release, and you have confirmed you will upgrade to implement the fix.

AFFECTED INSTANCES: vrtxsbx (SNC Instance - vrtxsbx).

ISSUE:

  • Genius Results (AI Search) on the /myvrtx portal were truncated when response streaming was enabled — the "Show More Information" option failed to render. Answers would cut off mid-response, sporadically and inconsistently.

main.Description:
A catalog item name is "Records Management Request". How can we bring it to the search result in the portal?
1. TEST instance (Australia release)
a. Commit the update sets to create the new catalog item.
b. Goto portal https://centerpointenergytest.service-now.com/ess_portal?id=cnp_ec_dashboard and search "Records Management Request" under "Ho can we help?". The new catalog item does not list in the search result even it showed up in "My Recent Items".

main.Resolution notes:
Hello Fran,

We are placing this case in a Solution Proposed state as per below information.

AFFECTED INSTANCES: centerpointenergytest.

ISSUE: Search a new catalog item does not work properly in TEST instance.

SOLUTION PROPOSED:
1) I noticed that the same issue started happening on the 'centerpointenergysandbox' instance as well after it was upgraded from Yokohama to Australia.

2) Upon detailed investigation, we found that the 'sc_category' record associated with the catalog item was inactive.
So we activated below record:
https://centerpointenergysandbox.service-now.com/sc_category_list.do?sysparm_query=title%3DSecurity%20and%20Access&sysparm_view=

And now the "Records Management Request" cat item is available in the search results in the ESS portal.

3) To fix the same on 'centerpointenergytest', please set the 'Active' field to True for below record:
https://centerpointenergytest.service-now.com/sc_category.do?sys_id=d2f7cae4c611227a018ddc481b34e099

Summary:
A single catalog item ("Records Management Request", sc_cat_item 18179af51bb6f2108cb70fa1604bcb13) stopped appearing in AI Search on Employee Center after an upgrade from Yokohama to Australia. The item was correctly indexed the whole time. It was being retrieved from the index and then silently removed during post-query security processing, because its primary category (Security and Access) was inactive.

Nothing was misconfigured by the upgrade. The inactive category had been there all along. Yokohama simply could not see it: catalog security ran as a pre-query filter that had no access to category state. From Zurich onward it runs as a post-query check that calls live Java on the category object, and an inactive category fails that check.

Late binding lets the search run unfiltered, then evaluates each returned document by calling live Java on the catalog item and its category. It inherits every check canView() performs, including active.

Fix: activating the Security and Access category record restored the item to search results immediately. No reindex required (APPLIED ON SANDBOX - centerpointenergysandbox)

For more information on same, please refer to below KB:
https://support.servicenow.com/kb?id=kb_article_view&sysparm_article=KB2774473

main.Subject: There is no Meta field on Policy record level
main.Description: It's recommended to use Meta field on Knowledge article to improve quality of AI search. We are wondering how to address it in the context of Policies. Policy authors are not working on Knowledge level to populate Meta field and there is no place to put keywords that can be copied to the related published article in the Meta field. Do we need to create custom solution to have Meta field on Policy level? Are there any best practices?
main.Resolution notes:
Hello Natallia,

My name is Ashish Singh, and I have been assigned to assist you with this case. Please find my comments below regarding your query:

The Meta field is available on the published Knowledge Article and is used by AI Search to help improve search relevance by matching keywords and tags. ServiceNow also recommends using metadata, tags, and keywords on Knowledge Articles to make content easier to find.Currently, there is no oob Meta field available on the Policy record. Because of this, policy authors cannot enter keywords at the Policy level and have them automatically copied to the related Knowledge Article. 

As a best practice, we recommend reviewing your publishing process and managing keywords, tags, and metadata directly on the Knowledge Article, since AI Search uses the article content, title, tags, and metadata when determining search relevance.If there is a business requirement for policy authors to maintain keywords before publication and automatically transfer them to the Knowledge Article, this would require a custom solution. However, that would be a customization of the business process rather than a standard AI Search or Policy Management feature. 

From a Support perspective, our scope is limited to break-fix assistance for existing product functionality. I apologise that we are unable to provide design or implementation guidance for this requirement.
For further advice on best practices, implementation options, or potential custom solutions, I would recommend reaching out to your Solution Consultant, Peter Meert, who is associated with your account.

I apologise again that we could not be of more help with this request and appreciate your understanding.

Next step:
Please accept the solution to close the case if issue is fixed.
Once this case is closed, a survey will be automatically sent to you. We kindly ask that you take a moment to share your feedback on our service. Your input is invaluable in helping us maintain and improve the quality of support we provide.


Thanks,
Ashish Singh, Sr Technical Support Engineer - PT
